It's a [[compelling]] read — I finished it in a day.
There's no [[compelling]] reason to switch vendors.
The quote was [[compelling]] because the nurse named the hours she got back.
I didn't have a [[compelling]] reason to stay for a third interview.

contrast.note_zh: convincing 是论据足以让人接受；compelling 更强：有拉力，让人很难不理会
interesting 只是有意思；compelling 是内容/理由强到会推动你采取行动

examples_stage_b: QR codes became [[ubiquitous]] during the pandemic.
Coffee chains are [[ubiquitous]] in this city.
AI tools are fast becoming [[ubiquitous]] at work.
Earbuds are [[ubiquitous]] on the morning train.
Once the chat widget became [[ubiquitous]], the help desk stopped picking up.

contrast.note_zh: common 是常见、普通；ubiquitous 强调到处都是、几乎躲不开
popular 是受欢迎；ubiquitous 不评价好坏，只说覆盖面已经铺开

examples_stage_b: The deadline seems [[arbitrary]] — can we move it?
Pick an [[arbitrary]] number to start.
Staff resent [[arbitrary]] decisions from above.
The seating chart felt [[arbitrary]]; nobody could say why table four existed.
Don't ship an [[arbitrary]] character limit — tie it to the text-message cap.

contrast.note_zh: random 是无规律、碰巧；arbitrary 强调由人武断拍板、缺乏合理依据
unfair 是不公平；arbitrary 先说决策没标准，结果才常常显得不公平

examples_stage_b: Can I be [[candid]] about the proposal?
She gave a [[candid]] interview about burnout.
I appreciate [[candid]] feedback, even when it stings.
I'll be [[candid]]: we missed the number, and the pipeline won't save the quarter.
A [[candid]] note to the host beats disappearing on the dinner.

contrast.note_zh: honest 是不撒谎、品行正直；candid 强调当面直言、不绕弯，哪怕不中听
frank 也是直说；candid 更常用于反馈/访谈里「我把真实看法摊开」

examples_stage_b: Her notes are [[meticulous]].
The audit requires [[meticulous]] record-keeping.
He planned the trip with [[meticulous]] care.
The lab tech was [[meticulous]] about labeling every sample twice.
[[Meticulous]] packing is why the camera survived the overhead bin.

contrast.note_zh: careful 泛指小心；meticulous 强调对细节极度认真，几乎不放过差错
prudent 偏判断审慎、规避风险；meticulous 偏执行时把细节做到位

gloss_zh: 有韧性的；能迅速恢复的
examples_stage_b: Our supply chain needs to be more [[resilient]].
The economy proved [[resilient]] despite rate hikes.
She's [[resilient]] — she bounced back fast.
The crew stayed [[resilient]] when the launch slipped and the press still came.
Kids can be [[resilient]], and a new school in March is still a lot.

contrast.note_zh: tough 偏能扛、强硬；resilient 强调受挫后能弹回来、恢复
strong 泛指强；resilient 看的是冲击之后能不能回到可用状态

examples_stage_b: Fax machines are nearly [[obsolete]].
New rules made the old contract [[obsolete]].
Will this skill become [[obsolete]] in ten years?
The pager system is [[obsolete]]; the ward uses the app now.
That plugin went [[obsolete]] the week the browser dropped the old API.

contrast.note_zh: old 只是年代久；obsolete 是已被更好的东西取代、不再能用
outdated 是过时了；obsolete 更彻底：基本没人再采用、系统里也该淘汰

examples_stage_b: An open office isn't [[conducive]] to deep work.
Low rates are [[conducive]] to investment.
The quiet café is [[conducive]] to reading.
A shared kitchen isn't [[conducive]] to a confidential board call.
A same-day deadline is rarely [[conducive]] to a careful memo.
It would be [[prudent]] to wait for the audit.
A [[prudent]] investor diversifies.
It's [[prudent]] to book early in peak season.
It was [[prudent]] to keep a month of payroll in a separate account.
A [[prudent]] guest brings something small and doesn't rearrange the kitchen.

contrast.note_zh: careful 泛指小心、避免出错；prudent 强调判断上的审慎、规避风险（决策/投资）
wise 偏智慧、见识广；prudent 更具体：眼下这步是否稳妥、风险是否可控
meticulous 偏细节一丝不苟；prudent 偏是否该做、怎么做更稳妥

examples_stage_b: The tax rules are [[intricate]].
She wore an [[intricate]] silver necklace.
We untangled an [[intricate]] web of contracts.
The signup flow is too [[intricate]] for a nurse with six minutes.
He spent Sunday on an [[intricate]] model of the harbor bridge.

contrast.note_zh: complicated 是复杂难懂；intricate 强调零件/线索很多且彼此精细咬合
complex 是有很多部分；intricate 还带精巧、要仔细拆才能看清

gloss_zh: 难以捉摸的；难以达到的
examples_stage_b: Profitability has proved [[elusive]] so far.
The perfect work-life balance feels [[elusive]].
The cause of the bug was [[elusive]] for days.
A straight answer from the vendor stayed [[elusive]] all week.
Sleep was [[elusive]] the night before the hearing.

examples_stage_a: It had a [[profound]] effect on me.
examples_stage_b: AI will have [[profound]] implications for jobs.
She made a [[profound]] observation.
The trip left a [[profound]] impression on him.
Losing the anchor hospital had a [[profound]] effect on the roadmap.
The note from her teacher was short and [[profound]].
The new policy brought [[tangible]] benefits.
There's no [[tangible]] evidence yet.
Show the client something [[tangible]], like a prototype.
A signed order is [[tangible]]; a verbal yes in the hallway is not.
We wanted one [[tangible]] souvenir, not another tote from the booth.

contrast.note_zh: real 是真的存在；tangible 强调可感知、可量化的实在结果（不只口头）
concrete 偏具体、不抽象；tangible 更常说成果/收益能摸到、能数出来

examples_stage_b: The changes were merely [[superficial]].
He only has a [[superficial]] knowledge of finance.
Don't judge people on [[superficial]] things.
The redesign was [[superficial]] — new colors, the same broken checkout.
A [[superficial]] apology didn't fix the double charge on the card.
Good data is [[indispensable]] for this decision.
A power bank is [[indispensable]] when traveling.
No one is truly [[indispensable]].
A translator was [[indispensable]] in the Osaka meetings.
That one spreadsheet is [[indispensable]]; the others are copies of it.

contrast.note_zh: necessary 是需要的；indispensable 是缺了就转不动、几乎无法替代
important 是重要；indispensable 是这个角色/工具拿掉业务就断

examples_stage_b: Demand reached [[unprecedented]] levels.
The company faces [[unprecedented]] competition.
We saw [[unprecedented]] heat this summer.
The outage was [[unprecedented]]: four regions failed in the same hour.
She got an [[unprecedented]] stack of applications for a single seat.
His argument wasn't very [[coherent]].
Put these ideas into a [[coherent]] plan.
She was too tired to be [[coherent]].
The memo finally made a [[coherent]] case for closing the side product.
After the second glass he was less [[coherent]] about how to get home.

contrast.note_zh: clear 是清楚好懂；coherent 强调各部分逻辑连得上、不自相矛盾
logical 是推理合理；coherent 还要求整段叙述前后是一条线

examples_stage_b: We need a [[robust]] testing process.
Sales remained [[robust]] in Q2.
It's a [[robust]] phone — survived many drops.
We need a [[robust]] backup that isn't the same disk as production.
Demand for evening clinic slots stayed [[robust]] through the holiday week.

contrast.note_zh: strong 泛指强；robust 强调在压力/变化下仍稳、不易垮
solid 是扎实可靠；robust 更强调扛得住异常、波动和压力测试

examples_stage_b: Don't waste the meeting on [[trivial]] details.
The fix is [[trivial]] — five minutes.
What seems [[trivial]] to you may matter to her.
The typo is [[trivial]]; the missing signature is not.
To the chef, a cold plate is not a [[trivial]] complaint.

contrast.note_zh: unimportant 是不重要；trivial 强调琐碎到不值得花时间（别被它绊住）
small 只是规模小；trivial 是对结果几乎没影响，处理优先级应很低

examples_stage_b: The contract makes the terms [[explicit]].
She gave [[explicit]] instructions.
Nothing was [[explicit]], but we got the hint.
Please be [[explicit]] about whether the trip is reimbursed.
The card is [[explicit]]: one hundred eighty degrees, twelve minutes, then rest.

contrast.note_zh: clear 泛指清楚；explicit 是把话说死、不留含糊（规则、条款、指令）
implicit 是没明说但默认包含；explicit 是写在面上、双方没法装没看见

examples_stage_b: There's [[implicit]] pressure to work late.
Trust is [[implicit]] in this relationship.
His criticism was [[implicit]] but clear.
The raise came with an [[implicit]] expectation of weekend launches.
There was an [[implicit]] rule: you don't take the last dumpling.

contrast.note_zh: implied 是被暗示出来的；implicit 强调没写明但默认在里面（规则、态度）
explicit 是明说；implicit 是双方心照不宣、没写进句子里

examples_stage_b: Insurance helps [[mitigate]] losses.
We hedged to [[mitigate]] currency risk.
Planting trees can [[mitigate]] urban heat.
A staged rollout can [[mitigate]] the damage of a bad migration.
Shade sails [[mitigate]] the heat over the schoolyard at lunch.

contrast.note_zh: reduce 是把数量降下来；mitigate 是减轻伤害/风险的严重程度（未必消除）
alleviate 多用于痛苦、负担被缓解；mitigate 更常用于风险、损失

examples_stage_b: Constant delays [[undermine]] client trust.
He felt his manager [[undermined]] him in front of others.
Lack of sleep can [[undermine]] your health.
Leaking the draft [[undermined]] the negotiation before the first meeting.
Side comments in the channel can [[undermine]] a new lead faster than a missed target.

contrast.note_zh: weaken 泛指变弱；undermine 强调从内部/背后慢慢掏空信任或基础
damage 是造成伤害；undermine 更隐蔽：看起来没打正面，实则把支撑抽掉

examples_stage_a: It's hard to [[reconcile]] the two views.
examples_stage_b: We need to [[reconcile]] these accounts by Friday.
How do you [[reconcile]] ambition with family life?
They finally [[reconciled]] after years apart.
We couldn't [[reconcile]] the CRM count with what billing exported.
She was trying to [[reconcile]] the job in another city with staying near her parents.
She [[advocates]] for flexible hours.
Experts [[advocate]] regular breaks from screens.
He [[advocated]] a cautious approach.
The union [[advocates]] paid training time, not only a longer shift.
I [[advocate]] writing the decision down so we don't argue it again next month.
Analysts [[attribute]] the rally to rate cuts.
She [[attributes]] her success to good mentors.
The quote is often [[attributed]] to Einstein.
The write-up [[attributed]] the outage to a config push, not the database.
Don't [[attribute]] the quiet table to rudeness; people were just tired.
Can you [[discern]] any trend in the data?
I couldn't [[discern]] what he really wanted.
Readers should [[discern]] fact from opinion.
From the transcript you can [[discern]] who actually owns the decision.
I couldn't [[discern]] whether the smile was polite or pleased.
Hiring two more people will [[alleviate]] the workload.
Exercise can [[alleviate]] stress.
The new road may [[alleviate]] traffic.
A clearer menu would [[alleviate]] the questions stacking up at the counter.
The scholarship [[alleviated]] the need to keep two jobs.

contrast.note_zh: relieve 泛指解除不适；alleviate 强调减轻但通常不是彻底治好
mitigate 更常用于风险/冲击；alleviate 更常用于痛苦、压力、负担

examples_stage_b: Price hikes [[exacerbated]] customer churn.
Stress can [[exacerbate]] insomnia.
Tariffs may [[exacerbate]] inflation.
Adding a second tool [[exacerbated]] the confusion instead of clearing it.
The heat wave [[exacerbated]] the crush on the last train.

contrast.note_zh: worsen 是变糟；exacerbate 强调某个行为/因素把已有问题加剧了
aggravate 口语里也说惹恼/加重；exacerbate 更正式，对象几乎总是问题本身

examples_stage_b: We need data to [[substantiate]] the forecast.
He couldn't [[substantiate]] the allegations.
Please [[substantiate]] your expenses with receipts.
Bring the logs that [[substantiate]] a four-hour outage, not a screenshot of a chat.
A story doesn't [[substantiate]] the leave; the clinic form does.
Try to [[articulate]] what you actually need.
He struggled to [[articulate]] his feelings.
A good PM can [[articulate]] the vision clearly.
She [[articulated]] the risk in one sentence the board repeated later.
I couldn't [[articulate]] why the flat felt wrong until I timed the commute.
Please [[scrutinize]] the contract before signing.
Every expense will be [[scrutinized]].
She [[scrutinized]] his face for a reaction.
The auditor will [[scrutinize]] which deals we counted in December.
He [[scrutinized]] the menu for anything without dairy.

contrast.note_zh: check 是检查一下；scrutinize 是逐项盯着查、近乎不信任地审
examine 是认真查看；scrutinize 强度更高，常带质疑、找漏洞

examples_stage_b: Relations between the teams [[deteriorated]].
Margins will [[deteriorate]] if costs keep rising.
The weather [[deteriorated]] by afternoon.
Night-shift response times [[deteriorated]] after they outsourced the desk.
The paint [[deteriorated]] along the window that leaked all winter.
Good managers [[foster]] a culture of trust.
Travel can [[foster]] understanding between cultures.
The program [[fosters]] young talent.
Office hours [[foster]] the questions people won't type into a channel.
The Saturday program [[fosters]] kids who would otherwise stop at chapter two.
Red tape [[hinders]] innovation.
Noise can [[hinder]] concentration.
Lack of data [[hindered]] our analysis.
A twelve-step approval [[hinders]] a fix that should take an afternoon.
Fog [[hindered]] the ferry, so we drove the long way around the bay.

contrast.note_zh: prevent 是拦住不让发生；hinder 是拖后腿、让进展变慢（未必阻止）
stop 是停下；hinder 是造成阻力，事情可能仍在缓慢推进

examples_stage_b: Some firms [[circumvent]] sanctions via third countries.
We found a way to [[circumvent]] the bottleneck.
Don't [[circumvent]] the approval process.
They tried to [[circumvent]] procurement by calling the CEO directly.
A side door let guests [[circumvent]] the crowd in the lobby.

examples_stage_a: I [[concede]] that you have a point.
examples_stage_b: He [[conceded]] the plan had flaws.
We [[conceded]] on price to close the deal.
She refused to [[concede]] defeat.
The founder [[conceded]] that the first pricing page confused buyers.
I [[concede]] the trail was too long for the kids.

contrast.note_zh: admit 是承认事实；concede 常带不情愿：承认对方有理，或输掉一点
agree 是同意；concede 是让步式承认，并不等于整体站到对方那边

examples_stage_b: Analysts [[speculate]] about a possible merger.
We can only [[speculate]] about why he left.
He lost money [[speculating]] on crypto.
I won't [[speculate]] on the record about why the CFO left.
Neighbors [[speculated]] that the empty shop would become a bakery.
It's a classic [[dilemma]]: growth or profit.
She faced the [[dilemma]] of career versus family.
The ethical [[dilemma]] isn't easy to resolve.
The [[dilemma]] was whether to tell the clinic before we had a fix.
Picking a school in a new city is a [[dilemma]], not a tidy spreadsheet.

contrast.note_zh: problem 泛指问题；dilemma 是两难：选项都不舒服，必须选一个
issue 是待处理的事项；dilemma 强调没有干净的好选择

examples_stage_b: The [[paradox]] is that more choice makes people less happy.
There's a [[paradox]] in saving money by spending more.
Remote work creates a [[paradox]] of freedom and isolation.
The [[paradox]] of the tool is that it saves an hour and creates another meeting.
It's a [[paradox]] that the quietest person in the room wrote the sharpest note.
The whole plan rests on the [[premise]] that rates will fall.
I disagree with your basic [[premise]].
The movie has an interesting [[premise]].
We rejected the [[premise]] that growth requires a larger sales team.
The book's [[premise]] — a city that forgets one person a day — kept me reading.

contrast.note_zh: assumption 是未加验证就当真的假设；premise 是论证的起点，错了后面都不成立
idea 泛指想法；premise 是整套推理/计划建立其上的那条前提

examples_stage_b: Her career [[trajectory]] is impressive.
The company is on an upward [[trajectory]].
Small choices can change your life's [[trajectory]].
Losing one hospital can bend the year's [[trajectory]].
Night classes shifted his [[trajectory]] more than the name of the degree.
We found a [[discrepancy]] between the invoice and the PO.
Explain the [[discrepancy]] in your two statements.
There's a big [[discrepancy]] between price and value.
There's a [[discrepancy]] between seats sold and seats that actually logged in.
The scale showed a [[discrepancy]] after I moved it off the rug.

contrast.note_zh: difference 泛指不同；discrepancy 是本该一致却对不上（数字、说法）
gap 是差距/缺口；discrepancy 更指向两份记录之间的不一致

examples_stage_b: There's no [[consensus]] on the timeline yet.
The [[consensus]] among economists is a mild slowdown.
Let's build [[consensus]] before the board meeting.
We still lack [[consensus]] on charging per clinic or per seat.
The family reached a [[consensus]]: the holiday stays at grandma's.
Think about the legal [[implications]].
The [[implication]] was that I'd made a mistake.
This decision has [[implications]] for hiring.
The [[implication]] of a usage cap is that the busiest clinic will call angry.
I caught the [[implication]] and still asked her to say it in plain words.

contrast.note_zh: meaning 是字面意思；implication 是没说完的潜在含义或后果
consequence 是已经发生或明确的后果；implication 常还在「这意味着什么」

examples_stage_b: The survey has a sampling [[bias]].
We all have unconscious [[bias]].
The article shows a clear [[bias]] toward the company.
Survivorship [[bias]] made the case studies look cleaner than the full list.
The playlist has a [[bias]] toward one decade and almost nothing newer.
Data [[integrity]] is critical for this audit.
She refused the bribe, showing real [[integrity]].
Cracks threatened the bridge's structural [[integrity]].
We protected the [[integrity]] of the audit log even when it made the team look slow.
He edited the photo so hard it lost any [[integrity]].
Give the team more [[autonomy]] over decisions.
Teenagers crave [[autonomy]].
The region was granted greater [[autonomy]].
The squad has [[autonomy]] on the stack, not on the promise we made the hospital.
Moving out was about [[autonomy]], not about disliking the roommates.
Tax breaks are an [[incentive]] to invest.
We need better [[incentives]] for the sales team.
Free shipping is a strong [[incentive]] to buy.
A renewal discount is a weak [[incentive]] if the app still crashes on rounds.
The stamp card was enough of an [[incentive]] to come back for a fifth coffee.
The CEO's pay came under public [[scrutiny]].
The plan won't survive close [[scrutiny]].
Celebrities live under constant [[scrutiny]].
The pricing page will draw more [[scrutiny]] than the about page.
A second advisor put the thesis topic under fresh [[scrutiny]].
Strong sales led to [[complacency]].
There's no room for [[complacency]] in security.
After the win, [[complacency]] set in.
Early praise bred [[complacency]], and the second release slipped.
A quiet month is no excuse for [[complacency]] in a clinic's infection log.
I agree, with one [[caveat]].
The offer comes with several [[caveats]].
Big [[caveat]] — I haven't tested this on iOS.
One [[caveat]]: these figures leave out the pilot that hasn't been invoiced.
[[Caveat]] before you take the trail — it's mud if it rained overnight.

contrast.note_zh: warning 是提醒危险；caveat 是附加限制：可以用，但请注意这个条件
exception 是例外；caveat 是先接受结论，再补一句但书

gloss_zh: 上行空间；好的那一面、赚头
examples_stage_a: Where is the [[upside]] if price stays flat?
examples_stage_b: In IC I framed the [[upside]] as a second product line, not a richer price on the robot.
The founder kept citing logos; I asked what [[upside]] remains if the anchor plant never expands.
My note to the partnership: thin [[upside]] at this entry unless net retention clears 120 percent.
Counsel can argue the option pool, but our real [[upside]] sits in the next round, not this close.
On the reference call a buyer described [[upside]] as rolling the sensor from one line to six.

gloss_zh: 下行的一面；出事时亏在哪
examples_stage_a: What is the [[downside]] if that logo slips?
examples_stage_b: The [[downside]] I worry about is a down round that wipes the option pool.
I told her the [[downside]] of waiting is a rival signing the same hospital group.
Spell out the [[downside]] in the memo, not only the base case.
If the earnout misses, our [[downside]] is the capital already wired, not a lawsuit.
The staff engineer was blunt: the [[downside]] of that architecture is a six-month rewrite.

contrast.note_zh: risk 是可能出事的那个点；downside 是真出事时坏的一面有多大、我们亏在哪

examples_stage_a: I don't have [[conviction]] at this price.
examples_stage_b: My [[conviction]] rose after three plant managers described the same payback.
She has [[conviction]] on the team and none on the sales motion.
Please don't write [[conviction]] into the IC memo until the cohort file is in.
I can respect your [[conviction]] and still vote no on the entry valuation.
One design win is not enough [[conviction]] for a preemptive term sheet.

contrast.note_zh: confidence 是觉得自己有把握；conviction 是对这个判断信得深，愿意为之押注

examples_stage_a: Walk me through the [[thesis]] in one minute.
examples_stage_b: Our [[thesis]] is that factories will pay for the outcome, not for the model.
His [[thesis]] drifted once a second vertical started to look easier.
If the [[thesis]] only works with a subsidy, say that on page one of the memo.
I won't stretch price for a [[thesis]] we cannot test before year-end.
The board deck buried the [[thesis]] under twenty product slides.

contrast.note_zh: premise 是论证的起点，错了后面都倒；thesis 是这笔投资的整套逻辑，用来说服自己和合伙人

examples_stage_b: One [[red flag]]: the CTO resigned the week they opened the data room.
I treat a sudden change in revenue recognition as a [[red flag]], not a footnote.
The customer call surfaced a [[red flag]] — they are still on a free pilot, not a contract.
A side letter we had not seen is a [[red flag]] for me, even if the headline price is fine.
Don't bury that [[red flag]] in an appendix; put it in the first paragraph of the note.

contrast.note_zh: concern 是顾虑，还可以谈；red flag 是危险信号，你会停下来查，严重时直接放弃

gloss_zh: 一上来就行不通；不值得往下谈
examples_stage_b: Asking us to waive information rights is a [[non-starter]] for this fund.
That closing date is a [[non-starter]]; our IC does not meet again until the 18th.
I told counsel a full ratchet is a [[non-starter]], so don't spend the weekend on it.
For the founder, moving the HQ before the round closes is a [[non-starter]].
Calling it a 'strategic' with no check and a board seat is a [[non-starter]] on our side.

contrast.note_zh: deal-breaker 是谈着谈着出现的底线；non-starter 是这个想法一拿出来就不值得往下谈

examples_stage_a: Can we [[dig into]] churn by cohort?
examples_stage_b: I want to [[dig into]] why the second hospital stalled after a strong pilot.
Let's [[dig into]] the gross margin bridge before anyone debates valuation.
The associate will [[dig into]] the cap table and send questions by noon.
On the customer call, [[dig into]] who actually signs the purchase order.
Don't just admire the demo — [[dig into]] how many hours a tech still spends on site.

contrast.note_zh: look into 是去了解一下；dig into 是已经在桌上，往数字和原因里再钻一层

gloss_zh: 标出来提醒（通常要人接）
examples_stage_a: I'll [[flag]] the side letter for counsel.
examples_stage_b: Please [[flag]] anything in the data room that changes the revenue story.
She [[flagged]] the churn spike in the appendix before IC sat down.
I [[flagged]] that we still need a customer reference from outside his home market.
Can you [[flag]] the related-party line so finance doesn't miss it?
He [[flagged]] the exclusivity clause early, which saved us a week of markup.

contrast.note_zh: mention 是提一句；flag 是标出来让人接，通常意味着有风险或有决定要做

gloss_zh: 瓶颈；整条流程卡着的那一点
examples_stage_b: The [[bottleneck]] is legal review on the master agreement, not the product.
If onboarding engineers is the [[bottleneck]], another logo will not fix the quarter.
She named one [[bottleneck]]: the founder still approves every discount.
GPU supply was the [[bottleneck]] through spring; pipeline was not.
In the plant, inspection — not assembly — is the [[bottleneck]] they want software to ease.

contrast.note_zh: problem 是某个问题；bottleneck 是整条链卡在这一个点，别的再快也没用

gloss_zh: 谁把这件事盯到出结果
examples_stage_a: Who has [[ownership]] of the reference calls?
examples_stage_b: I want clear [[ownership]] before we leave the room — one name, not a committee.
The founder still holds [[ownership]] of pricing, which will not scale past ten reps.
Put [[ownership]] of the data room with the associate, and copy me only on blockers.
Without [[ownership]], the security questionnaire will sit in a shared inbox.
The board asked which executive has [[ownership]] of the factory rollout, not which vendor.

contrast.note_zh: responsibility 是职责归谁；ownership 是有人把结果盯到底，不等别人推一把

gloss_zh: 对一下进度；碰个头把信息对齐
examples_stage_a: Can we [[sync up]] before IC on Thursday?
examples_stage_b: Let's [[sync up]] for fifteen minutes after you finish the founder call.
I need to [[sync up]] with finance on the wire instructions before Friday.
The two associates should [[sync up]] so we don't ask the company the same question twice.
Can the three of us [[sync up]] Monday and decide who leads the customer calls?
Email is getting messy — let's [[sync up]] live and then I'll send the recap.

contrast.note_zh: circle back 是稍后再回复这件事；sync up 是约一次，把信息和进度对整齐

gloss_zh: 正反相抵之后；算总账的结论
examples_stage_b: [[Net-net]], the pilot paid for itself even though the rollout slipped.
There are holes in the model, but [[net-net]] I still want to take it to IC.
[[Net-net]], waiting a quarter costs us the lead, and the price will not get kinder.
He listed six risks, then said [[net-net]] the team is the reason to lean in.
[[Net-net]] for the LP letter: pacing is fine, and we are not forcing a close.

contrast.note_zh: in short 是把话说短；net-net 是正反相抵之后，你到底站哪边

examples_stage_a: Let's [[park that]] until we see retention.
examples_stage_b: We're out of time — [[park that]] and I'll put it on next week's agenda.
Can we [[park that]] legal point and finish the round size while everyone's here?
I'll [[park that]] question and come back once the cohort chart is up.
The founder wanted to debate branding; I asked to [[park that]] and stay on pipeline.
[[Park that]] for the board packet. It does not change today's vote.

contrast.note_zh: take it offline 是换到小范围另聊；park that 是先把话题放下，会上先不展开

gloss_zh: 补齐背景，达到能讨论的程度
examples_stage_a: I need a day to [[get up to speed]] on the data room.
examples_stage_b: Give me the binder tonight so I can [[get up to speed]] before Thursday's partner meeting.
The new associate has a week to [[get up to speed]] on the robotics file, then she joins the founder call.
I can't vote yet — I still have to [[get up to speed]] on how they price the sensor.
Please [[get up to speed]] on the cap table before you talk to their lawyer.
He asked for the recording so he could [[get up to speed]] without another hour of slides.

contrast.note_zh: catch up 常是叙旧或补近况；get up to speed 是把材料补到能参与讨论

gloss_zh: 单位经济：单客或单笔能不能赚钱
examples_stage_a: Show me [[unit economics]] before we talk price.
examples_stage_b: [[Unit economics]] work in the Shanghai plant and break in the smaller cities.
If payback is fourteen months, the [[unit economics]] are fine for this sales cycle.
I won't take a growth story to IC without [[unit economics]] on one shipped robot.
The memo should separate blended margin from true [[unit economics]] on a new logo.
Contribution turns positive only after the install — that's the [[unit economics]] question.
I don't see a [[go-to-market]] a hired VP can run without the founder on every call.
The [[go-to-market]] shifted from self-serve to a direct team once deals passed $80k.
Walk me through the [[go-to-market]] for hospitals, not the one that worked for clinics.
A pretty demo is not a [[go-to-market]]. Who writes the check, and how do they hear about it?
We passed last year on [[go-to-market]], not on the model.

gloss_zh: （基金）还没投出、可以调用的资金
examples_stage_a: We still have [[dry powder]] for a follow-on.
examples_stage_b: How much [[dry powder]] is left if we lead this round at the ask?
Hold some [[dry powder]]; I don't want to be full before the B.
The LP update should say we are deploying, not sitting on [[dry powder]].
With reserves tight, [[dry powder]] for new logos is smaller than people think.
She asked whether [[dry powder]] in the opportunity fund can join a preemptive.

contrast.note_zh: runway 是公司账上的现金还能烧几个月；dry powder 是基金这边还没投出、可以调用的钱

examples_stage_a: Save room for a [[follow-on]] in the B.
examples_stage_b: This check is a [[follow-on]], not a new logo.
I'd rather reserve than spend the last dollar before a [[follow-on]] is even priced.
The partnership debated a [[follow-on]] and voted to support the insider round.
Without a [[follow-on]] plan, we get diluted the moment a growth fund shows up.
Her note recommended a small [[follow-on]] only if net retention holds through December.

examples_stage_a: We'll take our [[pro rata]] in the next round.
examples_stage_b: Did we waive [[pro rata]], or is it still in the side letter?
I want [[pro rata]] rights even if we don't lead.
Taking full [[pro rata]] keeps our ownership flat; anything less and we slide.
The company is offering [[pro rata]] to majors only, which leaves the angels out.
If the round is hot, exercising [[pro rata]] matters more than arguing fees.

contrast.note_zh: follow-on 是后续轮再投一笔；pro rata 是按你现在的股比跟，免得被稀释。follow-on 可以大于、小于或正好等于 pro rata

gloss_zh: 用自己的判断把这笔投资接下来
examples_stage_b: Would you [[underwrite]] this if the hospital pilot slips a quarter?
I can [[underwrite]] the team; I cannot [[underwrite]] that sales forecast.
To [[underwrite]] the growth, I need cohort data, not a logo slide.
She will not [[underwrite]] the round until the security review is closed.
If we [[underwrite]] it, we should be ready to defend the price in IC, not shrug.

contrast.note_zh: invest 是出钱；underwrite 是你愿意用自己的判断把风险接下来，为这笔结论负责

examples_stage_a: What is the [[path to profitability]] if growth slows?
examples_stage_b: I need a [[path to profitability]] that does not assume a miracle on price.
The board asked for a [[path to profitability]] by 2028, not a vibe.
Cutting the second office is part of their [[path to profitability]], and it is specific.
Without a [[path to profitability]], a big round just buys a more expensive loss.
Show the [[path to profitability]] on one page: which cost bends, and in which quarter.

contrast.note_zh: runway 是钱还能撑多久；path to profitability 是怎么从亏到赚，靠什么假设

examples_stage_a: The structure keeps our [[optionality]] on the next round.
examples_stage_b: A smaller check preserves [[optionality]] if the series B gets crowded.
Exclusivity for nine months kills our [[optionality]], so I won't sign that.
I like the [[optionality]] of a warrant, but not if it spooks the founder.
Don't spend the reserve today; [[optionality]] is the point of holding it.
Two verticals give them [[optionality]] if hospitals buy slower than factories.

contrast.note_zh: choice 是眼前的选项；optionality 是结构上留着以后还能选，现在不必做死

examples_stage_a: Treat this as a [[soft commit]], not a final yes.
examples_stage_b: I can give the founder a [[soft commit]] and still wait for Thursday's IC.
A [[soft commit]] is not a wire. Please don't tell them the money is in.
We collected three [[soft commit]]s and not one of them has cleared a committee.
Change the note from 'committed' to [[soft commit]] so legal doesn't overread it.
If the price moves up, my [[soft commit]] comes off the table.

contrast.note_zh: a firm yes 是拍板，可以往下排；soft commit 是意向，IC 或条款变了还可以收回

gloss_zh: 优先清算权：退出时谁先拿回多少
examples_stage_b: A 2x participating [[liquidation preference]] is how this deal gets ugly in a small sale.
Please model the [[liquidation preference]] at a $40 million exit, not only at the dream number.
I will accept a 1x [[liquidation preference]] and I will not stack a second one on top.
Founders feel the [[liquidation preference]] only when the company sells for less than the raise.
Ask counsel whether the [[liquidation preference]] is senior to the earlier seed notes.

contrast.note_zh: dilution 是股份被稀释；liquidation preference 是公司卖掉或清算时，谁先拿回多少钱

gloss_zh: 重大的；大到该改变判断
examples_stage_a: Is that miss [[material]] to the vote?
examples_stage_b: A two-point gross-margin miss is not [[material]] if the cohort still pays back.
Counsel says the side letter is [[material]] and has to sit in the disclosure schedule.
I don't need every bug — only what is [[material]] to a hospital signing.
The delay is annoying, but it is not [[material]] to whether we lead.
For the audit, '[[material]]' means a reader of the statements would care, not that someone complained.

contrast.note_zh: important 是重要；material 是大到该改变你的判断、披露或投票
significant 是统计或程度上显著；material 在投资和报表里更偏「大到不能忽略」

gloss_zh: 增量的；一小步一小步加上去的
examples_stage_a: This feature is [[incremental]], not a new product.
examples_stage_b: The revenue is [[incremental]] to the service contract, not a separate line they can lose.
I see an [[incremental]] improvement on yield, not a step change in the process.
Hiring one seller is [[incremental]]; opening a second office is a different decision.
Ask what is [[incremental]] if they win the plant — new dollars, or shifted dollars?
An [[incremental]] edit to the prompt will not fix a workflow the nurses already skip.

contrast.note_zh: small 是数量少；incremental 是在已有的上面再加一截，步子不大，但方向是往上加
会上常对着说：incremental 是小步改进；material 是大到该改你的判断

examples_stage_b: Demand from factories is real; demand from cities is [[nascent]] and mostly pilots.
I treat a [[nascent]] category as a bet on timing, not as a missing spreadsheet.
Their [[nascent]] channel — two resellers — should not be modeled as a mature motion.
The science is [[nascent]], so a five-year forecast is a story, not a plan.
It is a [[nascent]] habit: a few teams use it weekly, and most have tried it once.

contrast.note_zh: new 只是新；nascent 是刚刚冒头，需求或做法本身都还没长成形
early 是阶段早；nascent 更强调还在萌芽，连买家怎么采购都没定

gloss_zh: 有差异化的；买家分得清、愿意为此付钱
examples_stage_b: A [[differentiated]] workflow beats a slightly better model on a public benchmark.
If three rivals demo the same screen, you are not [[differentiated]].
The data they capture on the line is what makes the offer [[differentiated]].
I asked the buyer why they picked this vendor — that answer is the [[differentiated]] bit.
Brand is not [[differentiated]] until a purchasing manager can say what they'd lose by switching.

contrast.note_zh: different 是不一样；differentiated 是买家分得清你和替代品，而且愿意为此付钱
unique 常被说满，像全世界只有一个；differentiated 只要求在购买决策里站得住

gloss_zh: 粘得住的；用户或收入不容易走
examples_stage_b: A [[sticky]] workflow is one the night shift complains about when it goes down.
Logo count is vanity if the revenue is not [[sticky]].
The tie-in to the plant's existing software is what makes the seat [[sticky]].
I want to know whether the habit is [[sticky]] once the founder stops visiting the plant.
Free users can look [[sticky]] and still never become a budget line.

contrast.note_zh: popular 是眼下很多人用；sticky 是用了就不想走，收入留得住
loyal 多半说人对人；sticky 说产品或收入让人离不开

gloss_zh: 撑得久的；不靠一轮热度
examples_stage_b: I want a [[durable]] advantage, not a feature a lab will copy by summer.
A one-year contract is revenue; a [[durable]] one survives a champion leaving.
The margin looks [[durable]] only if power prices stay in this band.
Ask whether the retention is [[durable]] outside the first three design partners.
Hype is not [[durable]]. The install base might be.

contrast.note_zh: resilient 是被打了一下还能弹回来；durable 是时间拉长仍然站得住
robust 是眼下结实、经得起折腾；durable 是这个优势或增长能撑很多年

gloss_zh: 长期结构性的（不随短周期摇摆）
examples_stage_a: I think this is a [[secular]] shift, not a cycle.
examples_stage_b: Power demand from data centers looks [[secular]]; a single capex pause does not erase it.
Don't call a hot quarter [[secular]] until you have seen a boring one.
The [[secular]] trend is factories instrumenting every line, whatever this year's order book says.
A [[secular]] tailwind still needs a company that can sell. The wind is not the business.
Aging technicians are a [[secular]] reason plants will buy software, not a one-year spike.

contrast.note_zh: cyclical 跟着景气上下；secular 是多年的结构性方向，不靠这一轮热度
long-term 只是时间长；secular 是说驱动力是结构性的，不是周期

gloss_zh: 只是个例的；有故事，还不成证据
examples_stage_b: One excited plant manager is [[anecdotal]] until we see the renewal.
I like the color, but let's label it [[anecdotal]] in the memo.
[[Anecdotal]] wins are how a deck hides a thin pipeline.
The nurse's comment is [[anecdotal]] and still worth a follow-up call.
Don't let an [[anecdotal]] outage become a paragraph about 'reliability risk' with no rate.

contrast.note_zh: an example 可以是证据的一块；anecdotal 是在提醒你：这只是个例，别当成规律
data 能复现、能计数；anecdotal 是故事，好听，但撑不起结论

gloss_zh: 有实质内容的；不是空话
examples_stage_a: I want a [[substantive]] answer on churn.
examples_stage_b: The first meeting was polite; the second one was finally [[substantive]].
A [[substantive]] reply would name the cohort, not say 'retention is healthy'.
We owe the company a [[substantive]] pass note, not a one-line 'timing'.
Slide four is the only [[substantive]] page. The rest is scenery.
Save the [[substantive]] debate for IC; this call is only to book the references.

contrast.note_zh: real 是真的；substantive 是有实质内容，不是客套或空话
detailed 是细节多；substantive 是内容站得住、值得认真对待

gloss_zh: 暂定的；先这么放着，还可以改
examples_stage_a: Put me down as a [[tentative]] yes.
examples_stage_b: The Friday slot is [[tentative]] until IC confirms the agenda.
I sent a [[tentative]] hold on the calendar, not an acceptance.
Treat the close date as [[tentative]]; their board has not met.
Her [[tentative]] read is to lean in, pending the customer calls.
A [[tentative]] term sheet still moves the conversation; it is not a handshake.

contrast.note_zh: unsure 是人还没拿定主意；tentative 是这个结论、日期或承诺先这么放着，还可以改
rough 是粗、不精确；tentative 是先给一个可撤回的说法

examples_stage_b: Stay [[skeptical]] of logo slides that don't name a budget owner.
She was [[skeptical]] in the first call and warmer after the plant visit.
I'm [[skeptical]], not opposed — show me the cohort and I'll update.
A [[skeptical]] associate is useful; a cynical one just slows the room.
Buyers were [[skeptical]] that a model could sit inside their quality system.

contrast.note_zh: doubtful 是觉得多半不成；skeptical 是还没被说服，要看证据
suspicious 是怀疑对方有问题；skeptical 不是指控，是不轻易买账

gloss_zh: 简洁的；短，而且把该说的说清
examples_stage_b: A [[concise]] pass note is five lines: what it is, why we passed, what would change it.
Please be [[concise]] in the partner meeting — the appendix can hold the rest.
Her update was [[concise]] and still included the number that mattered.
[[Concise]] does not mean vague. Cut the warm-up, keep the claim.
The founder is sharp when he is [[concise]] and lost when he narrates the whole company.

contrast.note_zh: short 只是篇幅短；concise 是短，而且把该说的说清了
brief 也可以是短；concise 强调没有废句，信息密度高

gloss_zh: 有意的；想清楚再做、不赶
examples_stage_b: Skipping the second vertical was a [[deliberate]] choice, not a miss.
I want a [[deliberate]] process on price, not a number we invent in the taxi.
The tone in that email felt [[deliberate]] — he wanted the founder to feel the no.
A [[deliberate]] rollout to two plants beats a splashy launch they cannot support.
If the omission was [[deliberate]], we have a trust issue; if it was sloppy, we have a process issue.

contrast.note_zh: careful 是小心别出错；deliberate 是想清楚了再做，可以慢，但不是胆小
by accident 是碰巧；deliberate 是有意的

gloss_zh: 碎片化的；拆成许多小块、没有龙头
examples_stage_b: A [[fragmented]] market of regional clinics is hard to sell into and easy to consolidate.
Ownership of the data is [[fragmented]] across the plant, IT, and a vendor from 2016.
I like [[fragmented]] industries when the software can be the layer they share.
The cap table is [[fragmented]] — forty angels — which will slow any consent.
Search results on this category are [[fragmented]]; no single name owns the buyer's mind.

contrast.note_zh: messy 是乱；fragmented 是市场、数据或股权被切成许多小块，没有一家说了算
scattered 是撒开、不集中；fragmented 更常指本来可以是一整块，结果被拆碎了

gloss_zh: （市场）饱和的；该买的差不多买了
examples_stage_b: If every top-50 hospital already has a vendor, the segment is [[saturated]].
A [[saturated]] category can still have a wedge if the incumbent is hated.
I don't buy '[[saturated]]' while half the plants still run the line on paper.
Ads got expensive because the channel is [[saturated]], not because the product failed.
Once a tool is [[saturated]] inside one chain, growth has to come from a new buyer.

contrast.note_zh: full 是装够了；saturated 是该买的人差不多都买了，新增长变难
crowded 是玩家多、挤；saturated 是需求端接近见顶

gloss_zh: 被做成大路货的；没差别、只能比价
examples_stage_b: Once the API is [[commoditized]], the margin sits in the workflow, not the token.
A [[commoditized]] sensor still sells; it just doesn't earn a software multiple.
If buyers compare you on a spreadsheet of specs, you are already [[commoditized]].
I worry the core model gets [[commoditized]] before they own distribution.
Support and uptime are how they avoid being [[commoditized]] against a cheaper import.

contrast.note_zh: cheap 是价格低；commoditized 是产品被看成没差别，买家只肯比价
generic 是没牌子；commoditized 是曾经有差别的东西，后来差别消失、只能拼价格

gloss_zh: 催化剂；把变化点燃或加速的那件事
examples_stage_a: What is the [[catalyst]] in the next two quarters?
examples_stage_b: A signed hospital chain would be the [[catalyst]], not another conference demo.
The rate cut is a [[catalyst]] for the buyers, not a reason the product works.
I don't see a [[catalyst]] between now and the raise, so the round may sit.
Regulatory clearance can be a [[catalyst]] if the sales team is already in the accounts.
Losing the champion was a negative [[catalyst]]; the pipeline didn't die on its own.

contrast.note_zh: cause 是原因；catalyst 是把本来可能发生的变化点燃或加速的那件事
reason 是理由、整套逻辑；catalyst 多半是一个触发事件

gloss_zh: 悬着没落地、一直压着价格或决策的事
examples_stage_a: The lockup is an [[overhang]] on the price.
examples_stage_b: A large secondary is an [[overhang]] until those holders actually sell or commit to stay.
The lawsuit is an [[overhang]] on any exit, even if they expect to win.
Unsold inventory from the last raise became an [[overhang]] for new money.
I don't want employee-sale rumors as an [[overhang]] going into IC.
Until the earnout is settled, it sits as an [[overhang]] on the founder's attention.

contrast.note_zh: risk 是可能的坏结果；overhang 是一件还没落地的事，已经在压价格、情绪或决策
uncertainty 是说不清；overhang 是你知道那件事在（解禁、诉讼、有人要卖），它还没发生就在施压

gloss_zh: 只属于这家、这笔或这个人的；不能外推
examples_stage_a: That miss looks [[idiosyncratic]], not a market turn.
examples_stage_b: The write-down was [[idiosyncratic]] to one customer, according to the footnote.
An [[idiosyncratic]] founder dispute is not the same as a broken category.
Please say whether the outage was [[idiosyncratic]] or a pattern across plants.
The letter called the loss [[idiosyncratic]] and still didn't show the other accounts.
I treat an [[idiosyncratic]] explanation with suspicion until the cohort says the same thing.

contrast.note_zh: unique 常带褒义，像独一无二；idiosyncratic 是只有这家或这笔如此，不能外推到行业
random 是没规律、随便；idiosyncratic 是有原因的，只是原因不在整个市场

gloss_zh: 切题的；正对眼前这个问题
examples_stage_a: Is that clause [[pertinent]] to our vote?
examples_stage_b: Please limit the memo to facts [[pertinent]] to price and rights.
The historical mission slide is not [[pertinent]] to whether the cohort retains.
She asked which documents were [[pertinent]] to the security review.
A long biography of the advisor is rarely [[pertinent]] in the first meeting.
Only comments [[pertinent]] to the exit math belong in that section of the note.

contrast.note_zh: relevant 是有关；pertinent 是直接切中眼前这个问题，不是沾一点边
related 是沾边；pertinent 是讨论这件事时正该用上的

gloss_zh: 使不可能；预先把路堵死
examples_stage_a: This clause would [[preclude]] a small sale.
examples_stage_b: Exclusivity through June [[preclude]]s a conversation with the other bidder.
One missing consent can [[preclude]] the whole financing.
Their license [[preclude]]s training a foundation model on customer data.
Saying yes today does not [[preclude]] a smaller check if IC cuts the size.
A participating preference can [[preclude]] a clean outcome for common in a modest exit.

contrast.note_zh: prevent 是阻止某事发生；preclude 是使它成为不可能，常是条款或前提把路堵死
stop 是让正在发生的停下来；preclude 多半还没开始就已经被排除

gloss_zh: 后果会铺开的；以后还能感到
examples_stage_a: Missing the audit is [[consequential]], not a footnote.
examples_stage_b: A quiet change in revenue recognition can be more [[consequential]] than a missed quarter.
The board called the CEO search [[consequential]] and refused to rush it.
Losing that plant is [[consequential]] because three references sit inside the same parent.
Not every delay is [[consequential]]; this one pushes the raise into a worse market.
The opinion described the control weakness as [[consequential]] to anyone reading the statements.

contrast.note_zh: important 是重要；consequential 是后果会铺开，以后还能感到
material 是大到该改变你的判断；consequential 强调后续影响会漫开，不一定已经大到改投票

gloss_zh: 毫不含糊的；没有第二种读法
examples_stage_a: We need an [[unequivocal]] yes or no.
examples_stage_b: The customer email was [[unequivocal]]: they will not renew without the audit log.
I want an [[unequivocal]] statement from the lead that they are in at this price.
His note was warm and not [[unequivocal]], so I still don't know the vote.
Counsel asked for [[unequivocal]] language that the option pool is included in the pre-money.
An [[unequivocal]] denial in the minutes matters more than a verbal 'we're fine'.

contrast.note_zh: clear 是清楚；unequivocal 是没有第二种读法，不留空子
explicit 是说出来了、不靠猜；unequivocal 是表态本身不含糊，不能再解释成别的意思

gloss_zh: 被拖得很长的；旷日持久
examples_stage_a: A [[protracted]] raise will exhaust the team.
examples_stage_b: A [[protracted]] customs fight delayed the tool by two quarters.
I don't want a [[protracted]] argument about the option pool in front of the founder.
The audit became [[protracted]] once they found the side letter.
[[Protracted]] talks with the city pushed the plant opening into winter.
What looked like a two-week pilot turned into a [[protracted]] proof with no invoice.

contrast.note_zh: long 是时间长；protracted 是本来该结束的过程被拖着走
slow 是速度慢；protracted 是谈判、审计、融资这类过程旷日持久

gloss_zh: 尽管（书面让步，后面常跟名词）
examples_stage_a: [[Notwithstanding]] the pilot win, burn is still too high.
examples_stage_b: [[Notwithstanding]] the logo churn, net revenue in the memo still grew.
[[Notwithstanding]] section 4, the company may hire a banker for a sale.
[[Notwithstanding]] a strong demo, two directors asked for a slower rollout.
The letter said, [[notwithstanding]] early losses, pacing stayed inside the plan.
[[Notwithstanding]] the founder's objection, the board kept the 1x preference.

contrast.note_zh: despite 是尽管，口语里更常说；notwithstanding 是书面让步，合同和备忘里多见
although 引导一个从句；notwithstanding 后面常直接跟名词：notwithstanding the delay

gloss_zh: 给已有的说法再垫一层；使更站得住
examples_stage_b: A third plant visit would [[bolster]] the payback claim before IC.
The renewal does more to [[bolster]] the case than another advisor quote.
Signed purchase orders [[bolster]] a forecast that otherwise is just pipeline.
I need something that will [[bolster]] gross margin, not a softer definition of it.
The reference [[bolster]]ed the team and did nothing for the sales motion.

contrast.note_zh: support 是支持，范围很宽；bolster 是给已经有的说法再垫一层，让它更站得住
prove 是证明为真；bolster 只是加一把证据，还没到盖棺

gloss_zh: 基准情形；不靠英雄假设、你拿去承销的那一档
examples_stage_a: The [[base case]] does not need a second factory.
examples_stage_b: Underwrite the [[base case]] off renewals you have seen, not pipeline you like.
If the [[base case]] already misses our hurdle, the optimistic tab is entertainment.
I want the [[base case]] in the first five lines of the memo.
The founder's plan is a hope; my [[base case]] cuts price and slips the hospital by a quarter.
We can discuss upside after the [[base case]] survives a boring year.

contrast.note_zh: upside 是向上的空间；base case 是你默认拿去承销的那一档，不靠英雄式假设
bull case 是好的那档，你还愿意辩护；base case 是你真拿去定价的主情形

gloss_zh: 乐观情形；好，而且你还愿意为之辩护
examples_stage_a: The [[bull case]] is a second buyer in autos, not a higher price.
examples_stage_b: A [[bull case]] that needs three miracles is a wish.
I will defend this [[bull case]] in the partner meeting: the plant rollout repeats, and yield holds.
Don't build a [[bull case]] by stretching every cell a little.
Even this [[bull case]] has to name who signs the purchase order.
At today's entry price, the [[bull case]] still returns less than we told LPs.

contrast.note_zh: upside 是「还有好处」这一侧；bull case 是一套还能自圆其说的乐观情形，带数字、你愿意当众辩护
base case 是主情形；bull case 要额外的好事发生，但不能靠奇迹

gloss_zh: 悲观情形；差，但仍然说得通
examples_stage_a: Walk me through the [[bear case]] before we talk ownership.
examples_stage_b: The [[bear case]] is a stalled renewal, not the company going to zero.
If you can't say the [[bear case]] out loud, you don't own the risk.
Her [[bear case]] includes a down round, not just a slower logo pace.
That [[bear case]] still makes the fund money, which is why I'm still listening.
A [[bear case]] that is secretly your real forecast means the memo is flattering us.

contrast.note_zh: downside 是向下的风险、坏的那一面；bear case 是你愿意写进备忘的悲观情形，不是灾难幻想
base case 是你拿去定价的主情形；bear case 更差，但必须仍然说得通

gloss_zh: 投前估值；新钱进来之前这家公司值多少
examples_stage_b: Confirm the option pool sits inside the [[pre-money]], or the dilution is worse than the slide.
The founder quoted a [[pre-money]]; translate it into our ownership before Thursday.
A high [[pre-money]] and a tiny check leaves us as decoration on the cap table.
That [[pre-money]] quietly assumes a note converts at a cap we have not read.
I can defend the team and still hate the [[pre-money]].

contrast.note_zh: pre-money 是新钱进来之前的公司价值；post-money 把这轮新钱算进去。粗算 post-money ≈ pre-money + 新进来的钱

gloss_zh: 投后估值；这轮新钱算进去之后值多少
examples_stage_a: Our check over the [[post-money]] is the ownership.
examples_stage_b: She said [[post-money]] and the room heard the other price, so the ownership math was wrong for an hour.
On a 100 [[post-money]], fifteen from us is fifteen percent only if the pool is already in.
Don't compare this [[post-money]] to last round's number until you know which one last round quoted.
I care whether the next buyer can clear this [[post-money]], not whether the headline flatters us.
Put last round and this [[post-money]] on one line so the step is visible.

contrast.note_zh: post-money 含这轮新钱；pre-money 不含。用支票除以 post-money，才是你大概的股比

gloss_zh: 估值抬升；相对上一轮高出多少
examples_stage_a: The [[step-up]] from the seed is hard to defend.
examples_stage_b: A 3x [[step-up]] in eighteen months needs more than two new logos.
I can live with a modest [[step-up]] if we are buying ownership, not a headline.
Insiders anchoring the [[step-up]] is not an outside lead agreeing to it.
The [[step-up]] shrinks once you count the notes converting at a discount.
What operating fact changed to justify that [[step-up]]?

contrast.note_zh: valuation 是这一轮的价格；step-up 是相对上一轮抬了多少，不是价格本身

gloss_zh: 减值；把持仓的账面价值调低
examples_stage_a: We may take a [[write-down]] if the round prices below our mark.
examples_stage_b: The [[write-down]] was one holding, not a view on the whole book.
I would rather book the [[write-down]] now than defend a mark the next round will embarrass.
The auditors asked whether that [[write-down]] belonged in December.
A flat round with harsh terms can force a [[write-down]] even when the headline price does not fall.
Don't bury a [[write-down]] under 'portfolio movement' in the letter to LPs.

contrast.note_zh: loss 是已经亏掉的钱；write-down 是把账面持仓调低，股份往往还在，未必已经卖出

gloss_zh: 锁定期；这段时间里这些股份不能卖
examples_stage_a: The [[lock-up]] runs eighteen months after listing.
examples_stage_b: A short [[lock-up]] on a large holder is how a listing starts with selling pressure.
Employees asked whether the [[lock-up]] binds the tender, or only a public listing.
I want the [[lock-up]] written down, not as a hallway promise from the founder.
When the [[lock-up]] ends, expect some early angels to sell into whatever window exists.
Counsel is marking which holders sit outside the [[lock-up]].

contrast.note_zh: lock-up 是合同里那段不能卖的期限；overhang 是这件事（或诉讼、大额旧股）还没落地就已经压着价格或决策

gloss_zh: 变现能力；这笔资产多久、能不能变成现金
examples_stage_a: There is no [[liquidity]] here until a sale.
examples_stage_b: Secondary [[liquidity]] for early employees is a conversation, not a path you can model.
I don't want our only [[liquidity]] to depend on one IPO window.
The new investor asked about [[liquidity]] on the pref before raising the check.
A tender is [[liquidity]] for holders; it does not mean the business is healthy.
Tighter credit changed what strategics will pay. Their own [[liquidity]] got tighter too.

contrast.note_zh: dry powder 是基金还没投出、可以调用的钱；liquidity 是一个仓位或资产能不能变成现金、要多久
cash 是账上已经是现金；liquidity 是变现的难易，现金本身只是最容易的那一端

gloss_zh: 集中度风险；太押在一个名字上，它一倒就伤到整盘
examples_stage_a: One buyer at forty percent of revenue is [[concentration risk]].
examples_stage_b: The fund's [[concentration risk]] sits in a single robotics name we have already marked up twice.
I will not add while [[concentration risk]] is this high and the plant has no second site.
Geographic [[concentration risk]] showed up when three hospitals folded into one procurement office.
Put [[concentration risk]] on its own line in the memo, above the team slide.
Calling it focus does not shrink the [[concentration risk]] if that one logo leaves.

contrast.note_zh: focus 是你故意收窄、打得深；concentration risk 是集中到一个名字或买家，它出问题会伤到整盘

gloss_zh: 毛利率；收入减去销货成本之后还剩多少
examples_stage_a: [[Gross margin]] fell because the build did not get cheaper.
examples_stage_b: Don't fold services into [[gross margin]] and then ask for a software multiple.
A hospital discount that blows through [[gross margin]] is a pricing problem.
I want [[gross margin]] by product line, not one blended boast.
If [[gross margin]] only works in the Shanghai plant, say that before Thursday.
The bridge should show what moved [[gross margin]]: mix, price, or scrap.

contrast.note_zh: margin 没说是哪一层；gross margin 专指收入减去销货成本，还没扣销售、研发和管理
gross margin 扣销货成本；contribution margin 扣可变成本，看还剩多少去盖固定成本。两边口径不同，不要混着比

gloss_zh: 边际贡献；扣掉可变成本后，还剩多少去盖固定成本
examples_stage_a: [[Contribution margin]] turns positive only after install.
examples_stage_b: If [[contribution margin]] is thin, four more sellers make the loss wider.
Walk through [[contribution margin]] per robot before anyone quotes a blended percentage.
The board packet buried [[contribution margin]] under a chart that still counts free pilots.
I can live with a slow ramp when [[contribution margin]] on the paid cohort is already healthy.
Support hours belong in [[contribution margin]]; leaving them out is how a 'software' logo stays unprofitable.

contrast.note_zh: gross margin 扣的是销货成本；contribution margin 扣可变成本（常含实施、支持、渠道），看这一单还剩多少去盖固定开销

gloss_zh: 回本周期；多久把获客或安装成本赚回来
examples_stage_a: What's the [[payback]] on a new logo?
examples_stage_b: Fourteen months of [[payback]] is acceptable on a hospital sale; four years is not.
[[Payback]] blows out if an installer still camps on site for a month.
Split [[payback]] by channel. The partner motion looks cheap until you add support.
A pretty logo with no [[payback]] is a reference, not a business.
Count [[payback]] from the first invoice, not from the day a pilot was signed.

contrast.note_zh: unit economics 是单客或单笔整套合不合算；payback 是其中一问：多久把获客或安装成本赚回来

gloss_zh: 抽成比例；平台从流过的交易额里留下的那一截
examples_stage_a: What [[take rate]] do they keep on each order?
examples_stage_b: A twelve percent [[take rate]] works only if the merchant still earns after ads and returns.
The [[take rate]] slid once a larger marketplace threatened to clone the listing.
I care how the [[take rate]] is collected — on the invoice, or quietly inside payments.
Don't applaud volume if the [[take rate]] only holds for the first wave of sellers.
[[Take rate]] expanded because they added payments, not because they raised the fee.

contrast.note_zh: take rate 是从流过的交易额里抽走的比例；margin 是抽完、再扣成本之后还剩多少利润。抽成高不等于赚得多

gloss_zh: 按假设调整过的；还不是已经发生的账面
examples_stage_a: Show [[pro forma]] margin with the deal in, and without it.
examples_stage_b: The [[pro forma]] headcount assumes an acqui-hire we have not signed.
I will not underwrite a [[pro forma]] synergy that starts in month one.
[[Pro forma]] revenue that adds churn back does not belong in the model.
Label the column [[pro forma]] so nobody reads it as booked.
On a [[pro forma]] basis the plant looks fine; on cash it does not.

contrast.note_zh: actual 是已经发生的；pro forma 是按假设调过的，比如把收购并进来，或把一次性费用拿掉

gloss_zh: 工作假设；眼下先按这个往下做，以后可以改
examples_stage_a: Our [[working assumption]] is that IC sits on the 18th.
examples_stage_b: Label the [[working assumption]] on churn so a reader can swap it.
I'm fine proceeding on that [[working assumption]], and I want it revisited after the plant visit.
Three people are carrying three [[working assumption]]s about who actually has budget.
The [[working assumption]] on close is June; slip it and the cash math changes.
Don't let a [[working assumption]] turn into a fact halfway down the note.

contrast.note_zh: assumption 是一个假设；working assumption 是眼下先按它往下做、标明白、以后可以换掉的那条

gloss_zh: 往前站；在这个价格或这件事上更愿意支持
examples_stage_a: I'd [[lean in]] if the cohort holds through December.
examples_stage_b: Two partners [[lean in]]; the third wants the audit before a vote.
I don't [[lean in]] just because the round is moving fast.
She will [[lean in]] on the technical pair and stay cold on the sales hire.
He [[leans in]] when the buyer is a plant manager and the science is still ugly.
I [[lean in]] to leading this one, not to a small check beside a fund that will not do the work.

contrast.note_zh: soft commit 是还没走内部流程的口头倾向；lean in 是你这个人更愿意往前站，可以已经在说「我站这边」
conviction 是你有多确信；lean in 是你愿意往前站一步。可以 lean in 而确信还没那么满

gloss_zh: 从整体里切出来单独处理的一块
examples_stage_a: We need a reserve [[carve-out]] for the follow-on.
examples_stage_b: The parent will sell a [[carve-out]], not the whole division.
I want a [[carve-out]] from the pool so new hires are not funding an old promise.
Model the China JV as a [[carve-out]], or it swamps the US numbers.
Counsel marked a [[carve-out]] so a sale under five million does not need every consent.
Without that [[carve-out]], the participating preference eats the common on a modest exit.

contrast.note_zh: exception 是破例、开一个口子；carve-out 是从整体里切出一块，让它单独适用另一套规则，或单独成为一笔资产

gloss_zh: 嵌进模型或方案里；后面的数已经把它算上了
examples_stage_a: [[Bake in]] a slower hospital ramp before IC.
examples_stage_b: The model only works if you [[bake in]] the founder's unpaid selling time.
Don't [[bake in]] a second factory until the first has a full quarter of output.
I [[baked in]] the audit cost and the round still clears our hurdle.
If legal fees are not [[baked in]], the use of proceeds is a story.
[[Bake in]] the renewal discount before you show me the return.

contrast.note_zh: assume 是先当作真；bake in 是写进模型或方案里，后面的数字已经把它算进去了

gloss_zh: 把数字清一遍；去掉重复、一次性和对不上的
examples_stage_a: [[Scrub]] the pipeline before it hits the memo.
examples_stage_b: Have her [[scrub]] any logo with no live user in ninety days.
I [[scrubbed]] the bridge and two 'expansions' were prepaid services.
Please [[scrub]] one-time installation fees out of the run-rate.
[[Scrub]] the cap table for side letters before we debate who owns what.
A figure nobody has [[scrubbed]] does not belong on slide one.

contrast.note_zh: dig into 是往原因里钻；scrub 是把数字滤一遍，去掉重复、一次性和对不上的
sanity-check 是快速看离谱不离谱；scrub 是认真清一遍，花的时间更长

gloss_zh: 快速核对；先看这个数离谱不离谱
examples_stage_a: Can we [[sanity-check]] the cohort before Thursday?
examples_stage_b: [[Sanity-check]] the market slide against how many plants actually buy this tool.
I [[sanity-checked]] hiring against cash. It breaks in month fourteen.
Ask finance to [[sanity-check]] the wire amount against the cap table, not against the email.
[[Sanity-check]] whether 'forty percent growth' is more logos or higher price.
The early bars are three customers. [[Sanity-check]] that before anyone says 'pattern'.

contrast.note_zh: sanity-check 是快看一眼算不算离谱；scrub 是把账认真清一遍。先 sanity-check，过不了就不必 scrub

gloss_zh: 敢拍板的；把事情定下来，不悬着
examples_stage_a: Be [[decisive]] on price. The rest can wait.
examples_stage_b: A [[decisive]] no on Tuesday saves the founder a month of pretend momentum.
The board was briefed and not [[decisive]], so the search drifted.
I want a [[decisive]] call on whether we lead or we follow.
She is [[decisive]] once the evidence is in, and slow while it is still stories.
Once the customer calls agree, be [[decisive]]. Don't open another loop.

contrast.note_zh: confident 是你觉得有把握；decisive 是你把决定做了，事情不再悬着。有把握却不拍板，就不算 decisive
assertive 是把立场说清楚；decisive 是把板拍了。可以很 assertive，会还是没散

gloss_zh: 立场清楚的；说得坚定，但不压人
examples_stage_a: Be [[assertive]] on the pool, not apologetic.
examples_stage_b: An [[assertive]] question about churn is not an attack.
He was [[assertive]] with the banker and polite with the founder. That split was right.
I want the memo [[assertive]] about what would make us pass.
[[Assertive]] does not mean you raise your voice.
She got the protective provisions by being [[assertive]] early, before the draft hardened.

contrast.note_zh: pushy 是逼人、不给空间；assertive 是立场清楚、语气坚定，但不压对方
decisive 是拍板；assertive 是把看法说清楚。会可以很 assertive，决定仍留到下周

gloss_zh: 有分寸的；语气和步调收着，不冲
examples_stage_a: Keep the tone [[measured]] when you deliver the no.
examples_stage_b: A [[measured]] note to LPs beats a victory lap we have to walk back.
He stayed [[measured]] while the founder talked past the risks.
I want a [[measured]] recommendation: lead, follow, or pass, and the reason.
[[Measured]] is not vague. You can be calm and still be specific.
The email should sound [[measured]] even where the conclusion is a pass.

contrast.note_zh: careful 是怕出错；measured 是语气和步调有控制，可以照样把硬结论说出来
blunt 是不垫软话；measured 是收着说。同一个 no，可以 measured，也可以 blunt

gloss_zh: 直说的；不垫软话，可以偏硬
examples_stage_a: I'll be [[blunt]]: this price does not work for us.
examples_stage_b: A [[blunt]] pass is kinder than three weeks of soft maybes.
She was [[blunt]] about the sales hire and careful about the science.
Give me the [[blunt]] version in the room, and a calmer version in the LP letter.
[[Blunt]] comments on the deck saved Thursday from a fuzzy story.
[[Blunt]] is not careless. Cut the cushion, keep the facts.

contrast.note_zh: candid 是把真实看法摊开，可以仍然客气；blunt 是不垫软话，听着更硬
rude 是不礼貌；blunt 是选择不包装，目的是让判断更清楚

gloss_zh: 只表方向的；量级对就行，不是精确数
examples_stage_b: A [[directional]] read is enough for a first meeting and not enough for a term sheet.
The interviews are [[directional]]: buyers care about uptime, not about which model sits underneath.
Give me [[directional]] confidence on margin — up, flat, or down — before false precision.
I marked those cells [[directional]] so nobody wires a decision off them.
If the only support is [[directional]], say that in the opening paragraph.

contrast.note_zh: precise 是准数；directional 只表示方向和量级，不能当最终数字拿去投票
preliminary 是还早、以后会改；directional 是精度问题：箭头对，位数不可信。一个数可以又早又只是 directional

gloss_zh: 初步的；还早，结论以后会改
examples_stage_a: This is a [[preliminary]] read, not a recommendation.
examples_stage_b: The [[preliminary]] cap table is missing the notes. Don't quote ownership from it.
I have a [[preliminary]] yes, and I still want two customer calls.
[[Preliminary]] notes from the plant: yield is real, the data hookup is not.
Stamp the model [[preliminary]] until finance ties out revenue.
A [[preliminary]] draft can anchor a conversation. It should not leak as a promise.

contrast.note_zh: tentative 是还没承诺、可以收回；preliminary 是阶段还早，数字和判断以后会改。可以很早，但方向你已经认
final 是定稿；preliminary 是还会改的初稿或初判

gloss_zh: 定性的；讲机制和性质，不靠一张表定案
examples_stage_a: The [[qualitative]] story is ahead of the numbers.
examples_stage_b: I trust the [[qualitative]] notes from the nurses more than the satisfaction score.
A [[qualitative]] edge in how they reach buyers can beat a small lead on a benchmark.
Don't hide a weak cohort behind a [[qualitative]] paragraph about the mission.
The [[qualitative]] piece I still need is who owns the budget, not how the demo felt.
We have [[qualitative]] comfort on the team and almost none on the repeat purchase.

contrast.note_zh: qualitative 讲性质、机制、人家怎么说；quantitative 用数字。会上两个都要，不要用一个代替另一个
anecdotal 是拿个例当证据；qualitative 可以是成系统的访谈和判断，只是还没落成表

gloss_zh: 定量的；用数字把判断钉住
examples_stage_a: I need this [[quantitative]], not another adjective.
examples_stage_b: The [[quantitative]] case is payback under eighteen months in two plants.
A [[quantitative]] claim with no cohort behind it is a sentence.
Make retention [[quantitative]]: what percent, over what window, on which logos.
Be [[quantitative]] on margin and humble on the total market.
The [[quantitative]] gap is pipeline coverage, not a mood about the quarter.

contrast.note_zh: quantitative 要数字；qualitative 要机制和买方怎么说。缺数字就别装 quantitative

gloss_zh: 写进结构里的；不是一次性的，也不会自己弹回去
examples_stage_a: The margin lift looks [[structural]], not a one-quarter mix.
examples_stage_b: Losing a champion hurts. A [[structural]] change in how hospitals buy is worse.
Call it [[structural]] only if the cost stays out after the promotion ends.
The [[structural]] issue is a single supplier for the chip, not last month's scrap.
A reorg is not [[structural]] until the new owner has shipped something.
Pricing power that survives a dull year is [[structural]]. A discount week is not.

contrast.note_zh: one-off 是就这一次；structural 是底层变了，下一季还在
中文都容易说成「结构性」。secular 是多年趋势、不跟短周期走；structural 是这件变化写进了结构，不会自己消失

gloss_zh: 周期性的；跟着景气上下，不是那条多年趋势
examples_stage_b: Fab orders look [[cyclical]]. The software seat beside the tool looks steadier.
I don't want a peak multiple on a [[cyclical]] upswing in factory spending.
A [[cyclical]] downturn can still kill a company with eighteen months of cash.
Separate [[cyclical]] revenue from the part tied to the installed base.
A rebound can be [[cyclical]] without proving that buyers can't live without the product.

contrast.note_zh: secular 是多年的方向，不靠这一轮热度；cyclical 跟着景气上下，热会来，冷也会来
seasonal 是一年里的淡旺季；cyclical 是跨年的景气循环，比如资本开支、库存、信贷

gloss_zh: 有纪律的；价格、节奏或储备定了就照做
examples_stage_b: A [[disciplined]] pass at a hot dinner is part of the job.
We were [[disciplined]] on reserves and sloppy on entry ownership.
I want a [[disciplined]] rollout: two plants, a written kill line, then the rest.
[[Disciplined]] does not mean slow. It means you don't invent a new rule for one logo.
The partnership is [[disciplined]] when Friday's hurdle matches Monday's.

contrast.note_zh: careful 是小心别出错；disciplined 是规矩已经定了（价格、节奏、储备）就执行，不因为热闹破例
selective 是挑哪些做；disciplined 是挑定之后按规则走。可以 selective 而执行很松

gloss_zh: 挑剔着挑的；不是来者不拒
examples_stage_a: We can afford to be [[selective]] this year.
examples_stage_b: A [[selective]] pipeline is twenty real conversations, not two hundred names in a CRM.
Be [[selective]] on sector instead of busy in every thin wrapper.
They were [[selective]] about design partners, which is why the references sound alike and true.
[[Selective]] on price and loose on the team is not a strategy.
The fund feels [[selective]] when unspent capital is the point, and frantic when it is not.

contrast.note_zh: picky 常带挑剔、难伺候；selective 是有标准地挑，不什么都做
selective 决定进哪些；disciplined 是进了以后价格和节奏不破例

gloss_zh: 防守型的；先护住下行，不一定看空
examples_stage_a: I want a [[defensive]] structure if we are not leading.
examples_stage_b: A [[defensive]] check keeps us in the round without betting the reserves.
The terms I'd accept are [[defensive]]: 1x non-participating, and real information rights.
[[Defensive]] is not bearish. I still like the company.
Be [[defensive]] on governance rather than pretending we run a founder-controlled board.
A [[defensive]] book still needs a few names that can return the fund.

contrast.note_zh: bearish 是看空；defensive 是仓位或条款上先护住下行，可以对公司仍然看好
opportunistic 是看到窗口就上；defensive 是先把下行护住，不追这个窗口

gloss_zh: 抓窗口的；不按原剧本，看到合适的就上
examples_stage_a: This would be an [[opportunistic]] check, not a new theme.
examples_stage_b: An [[opportunistic]] add makes sense if the price resets and the thesis does not.
I don't want a habit of [[opportunistic]] chases after every founder who had a bad quarter.
The round is [[opportunistic]] for us: a known team, a lower price, a short process.
[[Opportunistic]] money that vanishes after one check is not a lead.
We can be [[opportunistic]] on this name and still keep the price rule on everything else.

contrast.note_zh: disciplined 按既定规则走；opportunistic 是为了一个具体窗口加快或破例。窗口要说得清，不然就是没纪律
defensive 先护下行；opportunistic 是窗口来了就上，姿势更主动

gloss_zh: 单线的；只靠一个人或一条关系撑着
examples_stage_a: The relationship is [[single-threaded]] through one engineer.
examples_stage_b: A [[single-threaded]] pipeline can print a great quarter and still be fragile.
I get nervous when security review is [[single-threaded]] to a champion with no budget.
Multi-site rollouts fail when implementation stays [[single-threaded]] on the founder.
Don't call it coverage if every account is still [[single-threaded]].
She is interviewing elsewhere. That is what [[single-threaded]] looks like on a Tuesday.

contrast.note_zh: bottleneck 是整条流程卡在一个点；single-threaded 是只靠一条线（一个人、一个买家），线断了事就断

gloss_zh: 楔子；用来打进客户的那个窄切口
examples_stage_a: The [[wedge]] is maintenance scheduling, not a whole factory system.
examples_stage_b: A [[wedge]] a plant manager can buy without IT is how they get in the door.
If the [[wedge]] never expands, we own a feature.
I like the [[wedge]] into quality teams. I don't yet see the budget next to it.
The [[wedge]] produced three logos, and none of them has a second module.
Leave the platform for later. Show a [[wedge]] a buyer can approve this quarter.

contrast.note_zh: wedge 是打进去的那个窄产品或切口；beachhead 是你先占住的那块市场

gloss_zh: 滩头；先占住、再向外扩的第一块市场
examples_stage_b: A [[beachhead]] in two health systems is a start, not a national motion.
Define the [[beachhead]] as a buyer and a budget, not as a vertical adjective.
They took the [[beachhead]] on service speed. The incumbent still owns the install base.
If every [[beachhead]] logo needs a custom deployment, it will not travel.
Name the [[beachhead]] we are underwriting, and which segment is explicitly later.

contrast.note_zh: beachhead 是先占住的那块市场；wedge 是打进那块市场用的窄产品
market 可以是整片；beachhead 只是你先拿下、用来站稳的第一块

gloss_zh: 先落地再扩张；同一个客户里从小单做到大
examples_stage_a: Is [[land-and-expand]] real, or just a second meeting?
examples_stage_b: [[Land-and-expand]] counts only if the next purchase order has a different budget owner.
They say [[land-and-expand]], but every site still needs the founder in the room.
I like [[land-and-expand]] inside one hospital chain and dislike it when each clinic is a fresh hunt.
The board asked whether [[land-and-expand]] shows up in net retention or only in a story.
A pilot that never invoices is not [[land-and-expand]].

contrast.note_zh: wedge 是产品切口；land-and-expand 是销售打法：先落一小单，再在同一个客户里做大

gloss_zh: 飞轮；转起来会自己越转越快的正循环
examples_stage_a: Where is the [[flywheel]], in one sentence?
examples_stage_b: More routes make dispatch smarter, which wins more routes. That loop is the [[flywheel]].
A loop drawn in a box is not a [[flywheel]] until one turn shows up in a cohort.
Usage from every install is supposed to feed the [[flywheel]], and nobody trusts the labels yet.
I don't fund a [[flywheel]] that starts only after they are already huge.
Hiring more sellers to hire more sellers is a cost, not a [[flywheel]].

contrast.note_zh: network effect 是用的人越多、对每个人越值钱；flywheel 是整圈正循环，网络效应可以只是其中一环

gloss_zh: 网络效应；用的人越多，对每个人越值钱
examples_stage_a: I don't see a [[network effect]]. Each plant can buy this alone.
examples_stage_b: A [[network effect]] inside one hospital chain is real, and it is also narrow.
Data from every line making the next install smarter is the [[network effect]] they should prove.
Without a [[network effect]], a cheaper sensor wins on price within a year.
The slide says [[network effect]]. The interviews describe pain when switching, which is a different claim.
A marketplace with no second side yet does not have a [[network effect]]. It has a hope.

contrast.note_zh: scale 是你自己变大、成本下来；network effect 是用户之间互相让产品更值钱
flywheel 是整圈循环；network effect 是一种具体机制，可以驱动飞轮，也可以单独被拿来吹

gloss_zh: 转换成本；客户换掉你要付的代价
examples_stage_a: [[Switching cost]] is high once auditors know the system.
examples_stage_b: A long contract is not [[switching cost]] if the buyer can leave at renewal without pain.
Put [[switching cost]] in hours of retraining, not in a metaphor.
Low [[switching cost]] is why the pilot felt easy and the renewal felt optional.
Ask the plant manager what [[switching cost]] she would actually eat to leave.
Data trapped in their format is [[switching cost]]. A logo on a slide is not.

contrast.note_zh: moat 是护城河的总称；switching cost 是客户换掉你要付的代价，常常是护城河的一块，不是全部

gloss_zh: 复利式累积；加上去的东西还会再生出下一轮
examples_stage_a: The [[compounding]] is in the data, not the logo count.
examples_stage_b: I underwrite [[compounding]] when each install makes the next deploy cheaper.
Without [[compounding]], a good year is a spike we should not capitalize.
[[Compounding]] inside one hospital chain beats fifty cold logos.
What looks small in year one is [[compounding]] if the account actually expands.
There is no [[compounding]] in a services shop that resets every statement of work.

contrast.note_zh: incremental 是在已有的上面再加一截；compounding 是加进去的东西还会再生出下一轮

gloss_zh: 二阶的；不是直接后果，是后果的后果
examples_stage_a: The [[second-order]] effect is every other hospital asking for the same discount.
examples_stage_b: I care about the [[second-order]] hit to references if this logo churns.
The hiring plan ignores the [[second-order]] load on a founder who still closes every deal.
A cheap API is not the risk. The [[second-order]] risk is becoming a feature inside someone else's suite.
Separate the direct savings from [[second-order]] behavior, like nurses working around the tool.
Cutting price looks fine until you count the [[second-order]] damage to the next negotiation.

contrast.note_zh: implication 是这件事直接带出的含义；second-order 是后果的后果，不是第一眼那条

gloss_zh: 故意唱反调；把对面的漏洞问出来
examples_stage_a: Let me play [[devil's advocate]] on the champion leaving.
examples_stage_b: I want someone at the partner meeting to be [[devil's advocate]] on the payback slide.
Playing [[devil's advocate]] is not the same as talking yourself out of a company you respect.
She took the [[devil's advocate]] seat on price and still voted yes.
Ask the associate for a [[devil's advocate]] note before we fall in love with the demo.
I'll be [[devil's advocate]]: if the installer quits, what is left of the rollout?

contrast.note_zh: push back 是你不同意；devil's advocate 是你故意站到对面把漏洞问出来，哪怕你可能其实赞成

gloss_zh: 不重大的；小到不该改变判断
examples_stage_a: That variance is [[immaterial]] to the vote.
examples_stage_b: A rounding gap on the cap table is [[immaterial]]. A missing note is not.
Counsel called the side arrangement [[immaterial]], and I still want it listed.
If the miss is [[immaterial]] to cash and to the cohort, don't relitigate the quarter.
The footnote treats the related-party balance as [[immaterial]] to a reader of the statements.
Please keep [[immaterial]] bugs out of the IC note.

contrast.note_zh: material 是大到该改判断或该披露；immaterial 是小到不改判断。书面和审计里更常见 immaterial，开口多半说 not material
trivial 带点「不值一提」的轻视；immaterial 是一个门槛：读者或投票不会因此改看法

gloss_zh: 名义上的；或小到几乎可以当没有
examples_stage_a: The license fee is [[nominal]]. Services are the business.
examples_stage_b: They paid a [[nominal]] sum for the IP and booked it like a market price.
A [[nominal]] observer seat still costs hours. Don't describe it as free.
[[Nominal]] rent from the parent is why that margin will not survive on its own.
I read a [[nominal]] option grant as a signal, not as retention.
The title is [[nominal]]. Someone else signs the purchase order.

contrast.note_zh: small 是不大；nominal 要么小到可以当没有，要么只是名头，不是实权或真实经济

gloss_zh: 负担沉重的；条件苛，压在人身上
examples_stage_b: An [[onerous]] information right annoys the company every quarter and barely protects us.
Exclusivity this broad is [[onerous]] if it blocks a small sale we would actually want.
I won't sign an [[onerous]] personal rep just to join a crowded round.
The lease is [[onerous]] next to the headcount they really need.
[[Onerous]] language in a side letter has a way of becoming the real deal.

contrast.note_zh: hard 是难；onerous 是负担重、条件苛，压在人身上。开口多半说 heavy 或 harsh

gloss_zh: 似是而非的；表面说得通，其实站不住
examples_stage_b: A [[specious]] comparison to a public multiple is how price gets silly.
The logic sounds tight and is [[specious]]: it treats pipeline as revenue.
Don't shout at it. Show why the claim is [[specious]].
[[Specious]] precision — two decimals on a guess — should come out of the note.
The operating-system analogy is [[specious]] once you notice the buyer does not switch platforms.

contrast.note_zh: plausible 是说得通、可能为真；specious 是表面像那么回事，其实站不住。开口可以说 sounds right but isn't

gloss_zh: 敷衍的；走了过场，没有真正做进去
examples_stage_b: A [[perfunctory]] board pack hides the one metric that moved.
Don't do a [[perfunctory]] pass on security because the logo is famous.
His answer on churn was [[perfunctory]], so we booked another call.
A [[perfunctory]] customer quote has no budget owner and no before-and-after.
A [[perfunctory]] conflicts check is how a side letter surprises you at signing.

contrast.note_zh: quick 是快；perfunctory 是走过场，动作做了，心没在上面
superficial 是停在表面；perfunctory 是敷衍地完成这个动作。开口可以说 going through the motions

examples_stage_b: The extra review was [[warranted]]; the draft hid the exception.
A public apology is not [[warranted]] for a typo in an internal note.
Her skepticism was [[warranted]] after the date slipped twice.
Pausing the rollout is [[warranted]] until someone owns the handoff.
That sharp email was not [[warranted]] by a scheduling miss.

contrast.note_zh: justified 是这件事正当、站得住；warranted 是眼下这个反应或追问有理由，不是过头
fair 是公道、不偏；warranted 是有依据、说得过去。一件事可以 fair，仍不 warrant 这么重的说法

examples_stage_b: Blame in the postmortem felt [[unwarranted]]; the vendor missed the window.
An [[unwarranted]] guess about motive turned a scheduling note into a fight.
Calling the pilot a failure is [[unwarranted]] when three sites have not reported.
I cut the [[unwarranted]] adjective before the note went to the chair.
His confidence was [[unwarranted]] given how thin the interviews were.

contrast.note_zh: baseless 是完全没有根据；unwarranted 是这个力度或结论站不住，未必是凭空捏造
unfair 是不公道；unwarranted 是没有依据，指责或反应过了头

examples_stage_a: The memo [[overstated]] how ready we are.
examples_stage_b: We [[overstated]] interest because three friendly users sounded like a crowd.
The headline [[overstated]] the outage; only the export failed.
A polished demo can [[overstate]] what the operator still does by hand.
Her note [[overstated]] agreement. Two people were still unconvinced.
The risk section is fair. The opening [[overstates]] how sure we are.

contrast.note_zh: exaggerated 是夸张、添油加醋；overstated 是把程度说满了，方向可能对，判断偏高
wrong 是错了；overstated 不一定方向错，是说得太满

examples_stage_a: He [[understated]] how messy the migration was.
examples_stage_b: The summary [[understated]] the delay. It was six weeks, not a few days.
An [[understated]] tone landed better than a victory paragraph.
She [[understated]] her role, and the room almost missed who fixed it.
The appendix [[understates]] the exception by burying it under a calm chart.
Keep the note [[understated]]. The concern is real, and the drama is not.

contrast.note_zh: modest 是人谦；understated 是把事情说小了，或语气故意收着
quiet 是声音小、话少；understated 是内容上没把分量说满

examples_stage_b: Announcing a date is [[premature]] until the second site confirms.
I marked the recommendation [[premature]] and asked for the missing interviews.
Judging the new editor after one draft is [[premature]].
The celebration note felt [[premature]]. Legal had not signed off.
It is [[premature]] to retire the old checklist while the new one still drops requests.

contrast.note_zh: hasty 是赶、没想清楚；premature 是时机未到，哪怕你已经想得很细
early 只是时间早；premature 是现在下结论或动手还太早

examples_stage_b: A written recap is [[overdue]]. People are still working off hallway comments.
The performance conversation is [[overdue]], and silence is starting to look like avoidance.
That security review was [[overdue]] before the incident, not because of it.
An [[overdue]] reply is now the story, more than the original question.
The roster is [[overdue]] for a name next to customer escalations.

contrast.note_zh: delayed 是被推迟了；overdue 是早该交、期限已过，还拖着
late 是迟了；overdue 是这件事早该做，拖着本身就是问题

gloss_zh: 有保留的；yes 带条件，不是「有资格」
examples_stage_b: Support is [[qualified]]. We proceed only if the open questions are listed.
Her [[qualified]] endorsement still left the timeline open.
Put the [[qualified]] part in the first line, not in a footnote.
A [[qualified]] agreement still has a condition. It is not a full yes.
I heard a [[qualified]] no: open to revisiting, not open to this plan.

contrast.note_zh: unequivocal 是不含糊、不留口子；qualified 是有保留的 yes 或判断，条件还在。不是「有资格」
sure 是你确定；qualified 是大体同意，但保留还在。不要理解成 qualified for a role

examples_stage_a: She was [[emphatic]]: the date will not move.
examples_stage_b: The reply was [[emphatic]] where the earlier note had been soft.
Be [[emphatic]] about the boundary, and quiet about the blame.
An [[emphatic]] no in the room saved us from another vague maybe.
He turned [[emphatic]] only when someone suggested skipping the review.
The last line is too [[emphatic]] for a draft that still has open questions.

contrast.note_zh: unequivocal 是内容上没有但书；emphatic 是口气很重、把这句说得很死，句子里仍可以有条件
strong 是力度大；emphatic 是说得很确定，听得出你不打算再软

examples_stage_a: The question was [[pointed]], and it landed.
examples_stage_b: Her note was [[pointed]]. The second section answers a question nobody asked.
A [[pointed]] remark about the missing backup changed the temperature of the room.
Keep it [[pointed]] at the choice we have to make, not at who typed the slide.
