The [[pointed]] line in the minutes was that we still do not know who decides.
He stayed courteous and still made a [[pointed]] remark about the missing page.

contrast.note_zh: blunt 是不垫软话；pointed 是点得准、对着具体的那一点，话里有钉子
sharp 可以是锋利或聪明；pointed 是有针对性，不是泛泛地凶

examples_stage_a: Try a more [[diplomatic]] version of that no.
examples_stage_b: [[Diplomatic]] phrasing kept the client in the conversation.
[[Diplomatic]] is not empty. Say the constraint without the insult.
She found a [[diplomatic]] way to tell the chair the packet was late.
A [[diplomatic]] opening helps. The third paragraph still has to be clear.
He was [[diplomatic]] with the vendor and direct with us afterward.

contrast.note_zh: polite 是有礼貌；diplomatic 是把话说圆，意思传到了，又不得罪人
careful 是怕说错；diplomatic 是有意把棱角磨掉，让对方还能接着谈

examples_stage_b: A [[noncommittal]] "we'll see" is not a plan.
She stayed [[noncommittal]] until the draft was in front of her.
The note is [[noncommittal]] on purpose. We do not have the facts.
I would rather hear a no than another [[noncommittal]] paragraph.
The chair stayed [[noncommittal]], so the decision is not made.

contrast.note_zh: vague 是说不清；noncommittal 是听懂了，故意不给 yes 也不给 no
cautious 是谨慎、怕踩坑；noncommittal 是不表态，不是还在小心核对

examples_stage_b: Blaming the outage on the new hire is [[far-fetched]].
One angry email is a [[far-fetched]] account of why the launch slipped.
I cut the [[far-fetched]] picture of every office adopting this by June.
It is not impossible. It is [[far-fetched]] without a second source.
The motive he offered is the [[far-fetched]] part. The sequence is not.

contrast.note_zh: specious 看似有理、其实站不住；far-fetched 是牵强、离眼下事实太远，还没装成严密论证
unlikely 是概率低；far-fetched 是要绕很远才连得上，听着牵强

examples_stage_a: The silence after the question was [[telling]].
examples_stage_b: It is [[telling]] that nobody would name the approver.
The most [[telling]] sentence was buried in the last paragraph.
A [[telling]] detail: they described the buyer and never the person who uses the tool.
What she skipped was more [[telling]] than the slides she walked through.
The revision history is [[telling]]. The conclusion flipped after one comment.

contrast.note_zh: obvious 是谁都看得出；telling 是这一小点很说明问题，值得拿来下判断
significant 是分量大；telling 是这一处泄露了真实情况，本身未必很大

gloss_zh: 反应被压住的；幅度平淡的
examples_stage_a: The reaction in the room was [[muted]].
examples_stage_b: A [[muted]] response to a miss like that should worry us.
Keep the praise [[muted]] until the night shift has tried it.
The write-up sounds [[muted]] because the disagreement was edited out.
Interest looks [[muted]], not gone. People are waiting on the policy note.
His [[muted]] delivery did not match the deadline sitting under the calm.

contrast.note_zh: quiet 是安静、话少；muted 是反应或幅度被压住了，不是没发生
weak 是本身不强；muted 是被收着、被压平，底下可以并不弱

examples_stage_a: Once we send it, that note is [[irreversible]].
examples_stage_b: Taking the team off the old tool is close to [[irreversible]].
Treat the public line as [[irreversible]]. A clarification will not catch up.
A reversible trial is fine. An [[irreversible]] cut to the old process is not.
Removing the only person who knows the archive is an [[irreversible]] step.
Tell me which choices are [[irreversible]] before Thursday.

contrast.note_zh: permanent 是长期如此；irreversible 是这一步做了就改不回去
serious 是严重；irreversible 是方向锁死，不是程度轻重

examples_stage_a: She was [[instrumental]] in getting the review unstuck.
examples_stage_b: The field notes were [[instrumental]]. The slide deck was not.
He was [[instrumental]] in the first month and hard to find after that.
One interpreter was [[instrumental]] when the client workshop jammed.
Don't call the tool [[instrumental]] if people still keep a side spreadsheet.
Quiet prep the night before was [[instrumental]]. The discussion stayed on the decision.

contrast.note_zh: helpful 是有帮助；instrumental 是起到关键作用，没有它这件事成不了
important 是重要；instrumental 是这个人或这一步实际把结果做成了

examples_stage_a: I want a [[rigorous]] pass before this goes out.
examples_stage_b: The argument is tidy, and it is not yet [[rigorous]].
A [[rigorous]] read asks what we never checked.
Hold the method to a [[rigorous]] standard, not a theatrical one.
Her questions were [[rigorous]] without turning hostile.
[[Rigorous]] means we can show the path from evidence to the conclusion.

contrast.note_zh: meticulous 是细节一丝不苟；rigorous 是标准严，方法和结论经得起查
careful 是小心；rigorous 是按硬标准过一遍，不是只怕出错

examples_stage_b: An [[airtight]] timeline still left the motive unexplained.
Don't call the note [[airtight]] while one source is unnamed.
The logic looks [[airtight]] until the timing assumption moves.
Make it [[airtight]] on who decided, not on every side detail.
An [[airtight]] reply answers the objection instead of stepping around it.

contrast.note_zh: rigorous 是过程严、经得起查；airtight 是这套说法严密到抠不进缝
perfect 是事事完美；airtight 是逻辑或证据封住了，对方难反驳

examples_stage_b: She was [[reluctant]], then took the assignment anyway.
A [[reluctant]] yes from the operator is a warning, not a go-ahead.
He was [[reluctant]] to put the disagreement in writing.
I'm [[reluctant]] to add another reviewer this late.
The client is [[reluctant]]. That is different from opposed.

contrast.note_zh: unwilling 是不愿意做；reluctant 是不情愿、勉强，最后可能还是做了
hesitant 是犹豫、还没动；reluctant 是心里别扭，动作可以已经在做

examples_stage_a: Can we get [[granular]] on where the time went?
examples_stage_b: The summary can stay short. The backup should be [[granular]].
A [[granular]] split by site showed the delay sitting in one city.
Don't get [[granular]] in the opening. Save the breakdown for the appendix.
I need a [[granular]] account of who signed, not a blended story.
Her update was [[granular]] on exceptions and vague on the actual decision.

contrast.note_zh: detailed 是细节多；granular 是拆到很细的一层，能按小块看
specific 是具体、不笼统；granular 是颗粒度，把一整块拆开

gloss_zh: 给说法加上限定；不是「有资格」
examples_stage_a: Let me [[qualify]] that. Only the first site.
examples_stage_b: I [[qualify]] the yes. It holds if the exception is written down.
[[Qualify]] the sentence before it reads like a promise.
She [[qualified]] the praise. The draft is clear, and the evidence is thin.
He would not [[qualify]] the line, so we cut it.
[[Qualify]] "ready," or stop using the word.

contrast.note_zh: clarify 是说清楚；qualify 是给说法加上限定，把刚才那句收窄。不是 qualify for，不是「有资格」
explain 是解释；qualify 是加上条件或范围，让它不再听成满口答应

examples_stage_a: We may have to [[walk back]] the date we just gave them.
examples_stage_b: He [[walked back]] "final" after counsel saw the draft.
Don't [[walk back]] a clear no just because the room went quiet.
The second email [[walked back]] the certainty of the first.
If we [[walk back]] the scope, say what is still in.
She [[walked back]] the blame and left the fact standing.

contrast.note_zh: take back 是把那句话收回、当没说过；walk back 是收回或软化刚才的说法，常常还留一点
push back 是反对别人；walk back 是收回或放软自己刚说的

examples_stage_a: Can we [[reframe]] this as a sequencing problem?
examples_stage_b: [[Reframe]] the question. Not who failed. What we still do not know.
He [[reframed]] a personality clash as a missing right to decide.
She [[reframed]] the delay as protecting the launch, not as drift.
I [[reframed]] the ask: not more people, one person who can say yes.
[[Reframe]] it in the memo, or the old argument starts again.

contrast.note_zh: rephrase 是换个说法，意思不变；reframe 是换一个框来看，问题本身被重新定义
change 是把内容改掉；reframe 是换视角，让原来的判断看得更清楚

examples_stage_b: Repeated slips [[erode]] trust faster than one bad miss.
Open questions [[erode]] a recommendation even when the prose is calm.
Side agreements [[erode]] the process we just asked people to follow.
Vague updates [[erode]] the habit of writing decisions down.
Confidence [[eroded]] when the second source contradicted the first.

contrast.note_zh: undermine 更像削弱根基、从底下掏；erode 是一点一点被啃掉
weaken 是变弱；erode 强调慢慢、持续地被磨掉

examples_stage_a: Don't let a side issue [[derail]] the decision.
examples_stage_b: A late rumor [[derailed]] a meeting that had a clear agenda.
One loud objection can [[derail]] the write-up if nobody sets it aside.
We [[derailed]] ourselves by reopening a naming question that was settled.
The demo [[derailed]] into a tour of features nobody had asked to see.
Leave the personal history out, or it will [[derail]] the feedback.

contrast.note_zh: stall 是拖住、还在原题上动不了；derail 是整件事脱轨，方向被带偏
delay 是时间后移；derail 是离开原来要决定的那件事

examples_stage_a: The review will [[stall]] without a next draft assigned.
examples_stage_b: Questions [[stalled]] when the only person with the file left the room.
Don't [[stall]] a call that is already late.
The thread [[stalled]] on a definition nobody wrote down.
A missing signature [[stalled]] the announcement, not the work.
We are [[stalled]] on access. Pretending otherwise wastes the week.

contrast.note_zh: delay 是推迟到另一个时间；stall 是卡住、推不动，不一定有新日期
stop 是停掉；stall 是还在议程上，只是动不了

examples_stage_b: The public scolding [[backfired]]. People stopped raising problems.
A third approver [[backfired]] and slowed every small fix.
The joke in the memo [[backfired]] with the client.
Pushing everyone to sound certain [[backfired]] into a promise we could not keep.
Copying the whole list [[backfired]] and hid the one person who had to act.

contrast.note_zh: fail 是没做成；backfire 是这步适得其反，反而伤到你
worsen 是情况变糟；backfire 是你本来想解决问题的那一步反噬了

gloss_zh: 更重要；一边压过另一边
examples_stage_a: The risk does not [[outweigh]] the reason to go ahead.
examples_stage_b: Clarity [[outweighs]] speed on this note.
One unhappy office does not [[outweigh]] the same pattern at six sites.
The cost of waiting [[outweighs]] the comfort of another draft.
Her objection [[outweighs]] the cosmetic edits.
Say in the memo which factor [[outweighs]] the others.

contrast.note_zh: exceed 是数量超过；outweigh 是这一侧更重要，一边压过另一边
more important 是更要紧；outweigh 是你已经把两边放上天平，明确说哪边压过

gloss_zh: 从下面挖掉（价格或论据）
examples_stage_b: A casual "probably fine" [[undercut]] an hour of careful review.
A lower quote in the hallway [[undercut]] the price the team had just stood behind.
The footnote [[undercuts]] the confident opening.
Don't [[undercut]] the written recommendation with a softer version in a side channel.
An old promise [[undercut]] the rule we stated on Monday.

contrast.note_zh: undermine 是削弱根基或信任；undercut 是从下面挖，把价格或论据抽掉
weaken 是变弱；undercut 是用更低的一档把原来的支撑拿掉

examples_stage_a: The deadline [[constrains]] how far we can reopen this.
examples_stage_b: Headcount [[constrains]] the plan more than the idea does.
Say what [[constrains]] you, instead of a vague "it's hard."
A shared inbox [[constrains]] how fast anyone can answer.
Last year's template should not [[constrain]] a different kind of call.
Access rules [[constrain]] who can even see the draft.

contrast.note_zh: limit 是设一条上限；constrain 是把还能活动的空间限住，选择变少
block 是挡住；constrain 是路还在，只是框紧了

examples_stage_b: The interviews [[surfaced]] a worry the deck never mentioned.
[[Surface]] the exception in the opening, not the appendix.
She [[surfaced]] the staffing gap without making it personal.
If we do not [[surface]] it now, it shows up as a surprise in review.
The questions [[surfaced]] a split between the two offices.

contrast.note_zh: flag 是标出来提醒别人接；surface 是让藏着的问题浮进讨论，不一定已经是警报
raise 是你提出一个议题；surface 是把已经在那儿、还没被说破的问题捞上来

gloss_zh: 先把问题或材料铺好，方便下一步
examples_stage_a: I'll [[tee up]] the decision for Monday.
examples_stage_b: [[Tee up]] the two options in the pre-read, not live in the room.
She [[teed up]] the disagreement so the chair did not meet it cold.
A short note can [[tee up]] the ask before the call.
Don't [[tee up]] six topics when we have time for one.
He [[teed up]] the evidence and then stopped, which helped.

contrast.note_zh: set up 是安排好；tee up 是先把问题或材料铺好，方便下一步马上接
park that 是先搁下；tee up 是铺好以便接着做，不是放下

examples_stage_b: [[Pin down]] the date before the invite goes out.
She [[pinned down]] a fuzzy "soon" to Friday noon.
I still cannot [[pin down]] whether the client asked or we assumed.
[[Pin down]] the scope in one sentence at the top.
He would not [[pin down]] the objection, so the debate stayed foggy.

contrast.note_zh: clarify 是把意思说清楚；pin down 是把含糊的说法钉死，要一个具体答案
ask 是发问；pin down 是不让它继续飘，钉成日期、人名或一句承诺

examples_stage_a: A public commitment today would be an [[overreach]].
examples_stage_b: The recommendation [[overreaches]] by telling another team how to staff.
I [[overreached]] in the room and narrowed it afterward.
A firm view helps. An [[overreach]] makes people stop listening.
Don't [[overreach]] on motive. We know what happened, not why.
The draft [[overreaches]] by calling a trial a new way of working.

contrast.note_zh: overdo 是做得过火；overreach 是伸手过长，超出自己的职权、证据或能力
ambitious 是有企图心；overreach 是已经越界，会反噬

examples_stage_b: She [[distilled]] an hour of argument into the actual choice.
[[Distill]] the interviews before the memo gets longer.
He can talk for twenty minutes and still not [[distill]] the point.
The appendix can stay long if the top [[distills]] the judgment.
[[Distill]] what would change your mind, not the whole history.

contrast.note_zh: summarize 是把内容缩短复述；distill 是收成几句真正的要点，其余丢掉
short 只是短；distill 是把长的炼成判断。concise 是说得短而清，不是这个动词

gloss_zh: 症结；真正卡着的那一点
examples_stage_a: The [[crux]] is whether we can support it after launch.
examples_stage_b: We argued about tone and missed the [[crux]]. The evidence is thin.
Put the [[crux]] in the first sentence.
The [[crux]] of her objection is timing, not the idea.
If you cannot name the [[crux]], the recommendation is not ready.
A long background section hid the [[crux]].

contrast.note_zh: bottleneck 是流程卡在那一点；crux 是论证或问题的症结，过了它判断才成立
point 是一个论点；crux 是真正卡着的那一点

examples_stage_a: There is [[friction]] between drafting and approval.
examples_stage_b: Most of the [[friction]] sits in the handoff, not in the work itself.
A shared template cut the [[friction]] without adding a meeting.
Name the [[friction]] before it hardens into a story about personalities.
The client feels the [[friction]] when we ask for the same file twice.
Some [[friction]] is useful. This kind only slows the reply.

contrast.note_zh: conflict 是冲突已经摆上台面；friction 是阻力、别扭的摩擦，还不一定吵起来
problem 是一个要修的问题；friction 是两边或两步之间不顺

examples_stage_a: [[Inertia]] is why the old checklist is still in use.
examples_stage_b: [[Inertia]], not a real dispute, kept that weekly meeting alive.
The plan is fine, and it is still losing to [[inertia]].
You need a named person to beat [[inertia]] on a process nobody likes.
Don't confuse [[inertia]] with agreement.
After the incident, [[inertia]] stopped being an acceptable reason.

contrast.note_zh: complacency 是自满、觉得不用动；inertia 是惯性，没人推就沿旧轨道滑，不一定觉得自己赢了
delay 是推迟；inertia 是根本没被推动，所以保持原样

examples_stage_a: We have some [[leeway]] on the date, and none on the facts.
examples_stage_b: The brief leaves [[leeway]] on format and none on the question.
Give the editor [[leeway]] on tone. Be strict about facts.
There is no [[leeway]] once the client has heard a date.
I can allow [[leeway]] on sequence if the decision itself stays firm.
Leave [[leeway]] in the agenda. The first item always runs long.

contrast.note_zh: optionality 是以后还能另选；leeway 是眼下这一步里还留的余地
room 是还有地方；leeway 是你被允许活动的那一点空间

examples_stage_a: There is a real [[tension]] between moving fast and keeping a clean record.
examples_stage_b: The [[tension]] is not personal. Both aims are legitimate.
Name the [[tension]] in the note instead of pretending it went away.
She held the [[tension]] and refused a false choice in the room.
A hiring bar and a deadline are in [[tension]] this month.
Skip that [[tension]] and the recommendation will sound naive.

contrast.note_zh: conflict 是要分出赢的一边；tension 是两边互相拉着，可以并存，还没爆
problem 是出了错要修；tension 是两种都说得通的目标在拽，不一定有错的一方

examples_stage_a: There is a [[mismatch]] between the ask and the draft.
examples_stage_b: The [[mismatch]] showed up when the client described a different problem.
Title and duties are a [[mismatch]]. The job is larger than the posting.
A [[mismatch]] in expectations caused the sharp email, not the typo.
The minutes are a [[mismatch]] with what we actually decided.
That cheerful tone is a [[mismatch]] for a note that is still unsure.

contrast.note_zh: gap 是中间缺一块；mismatch 是本该对上的两边对不上
difference 是不一样；mismatch 是尺寸、预期或说法错了位

examples_stage_a: We are at an [[impasse]] on whether to pause.
examples_stage_b: The [[impasse]] is about sequence, not about the goal.
Call it an [[impasse]] when another hour will not produce a decision.
A smaller question broke the [[impasse]]: what can go out without the new policy.
Don't cover an [[impasse]] with a vague action item.
The two offices hit an [[impasse]] and stopped answering.

contrast.note_zh: deadlock 是双方顶死、谁也不让；impasse 是谈到半路走不动，暂时没有路。stuck 只是卡住了
non-starter 是一上来就不值得谈；impasse 是谈过之后卡住了

examples_stage_a: That summary is a [[straw man]] of what she said.
examples_stage_b: Beating a [[straw man]] felt clever and settled nothing.
Restate her view before you attack a [[straw man]].
The slide fights a [[straw man]]. Nobody proposed skipping review.
A [[straw man]] is easier to knock over than the careful version in the memo.
If the objection only lands on a [[straw man]], it is not ready.

contrast.note_zh: devil's advocate 是故意唱反调，把对面问严，你可能其实赞成；straw man 是把对方简化成好打的假目标
fake 是假的；straw man 是把对方的观点换成一个更好打的版本，再拿来反驳

examples_stage_a: Staffing is a [[blind spot]] in this plan.
examples_stage_b: Ask someone outside the project. We share the same [[blind spot]].
The [[blind spot]] was the night shift, which never came up in interviews.
A useful reviewer catches your [[blind spot]] instead of rewriting the prose.
Confidence can hide a [[blind spot]] about how the work actually gets done.
The review named one [[blind spot]]: nobody covered the weekend on-call.

contrast.note_zh: weakness 是短板，你可能知道；blind spot 是自己看不见的那一块
gap 是缺口、缺一块；blind spot 是视野里的盲区

gloss_zh: 把注意力引走的假线索
examples_stage_a: The naming debate is a [[red herring]].
examples_stage_b: Blame is a [[red herring]]. The process never named a person.
One vivid anecdote became a [[red herring]] and took over the agenda.
Don't follow that [[red herring]] into the footnote.
Which tool we buy is a [[red herring]] if the handoff stays broken.
She called it a [[red herring]] and brought the room back to the decision.

contrast.note_zh: red flag 是危险信号，要停下来查；red herring 是把注意力引走的假线索
distraction 是让人分心；red herring 是看起来相关、其实把讨论带偏的那条线索

examples_stage_a: The meeting was [[ostensibly]] about the timeline.
examples_stage_b: He is [[ostensibly]] the approver. Someone else makes the call.
The note is [[ostensibly]] a recap. It reopens the decision.
We were [[ostensibly]] there to settle scope, and the hour went to old grievances.
The role is [[ostensibly]] advisory, which is why the signature surprised people.
An [[ostensibly]] small edit changed who is on the hook.

contrast.note_zh: superficial 是肤浅、停在表面；ostensibly 是表面上声称如此，实际可能不是
apparently 是看来如此；ostensibly 是对方摆出来的说法或身份，你留着怀疑。开口可以说 on the surface

examples_stage_a: The motive in that sentence is [[unsubstantiated]].
examples_stage_b: An [[unsubstantiated]] claim about intent does not belong in the minutes.
The rumor is [[unsubstantiated]]. Keep it out of the recommendation.
She marked the line [[unsubstantiated]] and asked for a source.
[[Unsubstantiated]] praise is as useless as a complaint with nothing behind it.
Without the log, the outage account stays [[unsubstantiated]].

contrast.note_zh: specious 是表面说得通、其实错；unsubstantiated 是还没有证据撑住，不一定已经证明是错的
unproven 是还没证实；unsubstantiated 是没有证据把这句话撑住。substantiate 是去拿出证据，这一条是还没被撑住

examples_stage_a: A [[cursory]] look will miss the exception.
examples_stage_b: The first pass was [[cursory]]. The objection is on page four.
Don't give the security pages a [[cursory]] glance because the rest looks familiar.
A [[cursory]] recap dropped the condition we had actually agreed.
He offered a [[cursory]] answer and moved on, so I asked again.
[[Cursory]] notes from the visit are not enough to judge the handoff.

contrast.note_zh: perfunctory 是敷衍、走形式；cursory 是看得粗、不细，可以是时间不够，不一定是态度敷衍
quick 是快；cursory 是粗看一眼，容易漏掉。开口可以说 quick 或 rough

examples_stage_a: The response should be [[commensurate]] with the miss.
examples_stage_b: A formal investigation is not [[commensurate]] with a typo in an internal draft.
The title is not [[commensurate]] with the calls she already makes.
Keep the tone [[commensurate]] with a process gap we can fix.
Another review is [[commensurate]] with how hard this is to undo.
The apology was not [[commensurate]] with the disruption the client felt.

contrast.note_zh: equal 是相等；commensurate 是和另一件事相称，量级匹配，不一定同一单位
fair 是公道；commensurate 是和这件事的大小、角色或后果相称

gloss_zh: 随之而来的推论或结果
examples_stage_a: A [[corollary]] of writing the decision down is fewer hallway reversals.
examples_stage_b: The [[corollary]] is uncomfortable: the old checklist has to go.
If the date is real, the [[corollary]] is that something else slips.
One [[corollary]] of the new rule is that hallway decisions no longer count.
She stated the [[corollary]] so nobody could claim surprise.
The [[corollary]] of waiting for a second source is that Thursday may move.

contrast.note_zh: implication 是这事的含义、会带来什么；corollary 是从前面那个判断紧跟着来的那一条推论
result 是结果；corollary 是顺着前一句几乎必然出来的推论。开口多半说 what follows
